specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:26:    "rationale": "Issue #1240 requires a self-service path from provider-local BYOM candidates to network offer/admission states without weakening signed catalog economics, route-time verification, receipt, billing, or payout gates."
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:33:SPEC-047 defines how a provider-local candidate discovered under SPEC-046 may be offered to the Malibu network and, after explicit checks, become eligible for network visibility, synthetic probes, buyer routing, catalog pricing, and settlement-capable paid traffic. Any synthetic probe is routed through the authenticated provider wire protocol or an admitted provider session; the coordinator MUST NOT dereference provider-submitted endpoint URLs, origins, sockets, or local paths.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:35:The user outcome is a self-service path for providers to discover, evaluate, offer, probe, and explicitly disclose more models without making Malibu the manual gatekeeper for every possible model. In v0.1, genuinely novel non-catalog candidates can become visible or probeable only under explicit non-earning disclosure; an earning path for non-catalog models requires a later billing-owner pricing conversion spec. The settlement outcome is equally important: positive provider credit still requires a route-time admitted snapshot and settlement-capable receipt profile governed by the money-path specs.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:43:SPEC-047 does not replace SPEC-005 billing formulas, SPEC-006 buyer API compatibility, SPEC-010 signed catalog identity, SPEC-015 receipt wire ownership, or SPEC-022 verified settlement.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:59:SPEC-005 owns billing formulas, rate math, provider rewards, settlement, and payout-ready ledger behavior.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:63:SPEC-010 owns canonical signed catalog identity. SPEC-047 may create network offer state for non-catalog candidates, but only SPEC-010-compatible or catalog-derived identities can satisfy catalog-verified settlement.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:65:SPEC-011 owns loaded-model state and warm-swap model-hash emission required before settlement-capable routing.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:67:SPEC-015 and SPEC-022 own receipt and verified-settlement conditions. SPEC-047 adds admission state; it does not by itself make a receipt settlement-capable.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:75:SPEC-044 consumes SPEC-047 admission state for Malibu economics UX when the app presents network-eligible or catalog-priced rows. SPEC-047 supplies admission state and does not depend on app presentation to enforce routing or settlement.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:86:**SPEC-047-R001 - Admission state machine.** Coordinator-backed admission MUST use a closed per-provider/per-candidate state machine with these v0.1 states: `not_offered`, `offer_submitted`, `offer_rejected`, `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, `withdrawn`, and `revoked`. SPEC-047 does not own SPEC-046 local states `local_only` or `offerable`; those states are CLI-only provider inventory states until a provider-signed offer enters the coordinator machine. State transitions MUST be append-only auditable events with actor, reason code, previous state, next state, provider id, candidate id, served model reference, evidence digests, timestamp, and request id. `settlement_capable` MUST NOT be reachable unless SPEC-022 verified-settlement preconditions are satisfiable for that provider/model pair at route time. No state transition outside this table is valid:
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:95:| `network_admitted_unsettled` | The candidate satisfies limited network admission checks but lacks trusted catalog economics or settlement prerequisites. | Keep the runtime healthy, satisfy requested catalog/receipt evidence, or withdraw. | coordinator admission policy | `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, `withdrawn`, `revoked` |
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:96:| `catalog_priced` | The candidate has trusted signed catalog economics for display, but it is not settlement-capable. | Keep the admitted model loaded and wait for receipt/route-time settlement prerequisites, or withdraw. | coordinator admission policy with SPEC-023/SPEC-044 trust inputs | `network_admitted_unsettled`, `settlement_capable`, `withdrawn`, `revoked` |
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:97:| `settlement_capable` | The candidate may participate in positive provider settlement only for request attempts satisfying SPEC-022 route-time snapshot and receipt verification. | Keep the loaded model, receipts, and health predicates current, or withdraw. | coordinator admission policy with SPEC-022 preconditions | `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `withdrawn`, `revoked` |
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:99:| `revoked` | The coordinator removed admission because policy, identity, artifact, health, sanctions, or settlement prerequisites failed. | Resolve the reason code and submit a new signed offer with refreshed evidence if policy allows. | coordinator policy, trust, or sanctions path | `offer_submitted` |
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:101:Re-entry from `offer_rejected`, `withdrawn`, or `revoked` to `offer_submitted` MUST require a new provider-signed offer with a fresh nonce or idempotency key and refreshed evidence digests. **[v0.1.9]** `offer_rejected` is RESERVED and unreachable in v0.2: no coordinator origin appends it (see §8 v0.1.5, "`offer_rejected` stated unreachable"), so this table lists its legal re-entry edge for enum completeness but the state is never entered and that edge is not exercised. The reachable fresh-evidence re-entry paths a v0.2 journey can prove are `withdrawn` and `revoked`. Demotion from `settlement_capable` or `catalog_priced` takes effect for routing and settlement before any later request attempt can be admitted under the older state.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:105:Any allowed next state that depends on trusted catalog economics, catalog identity, receipt capability, or route-time settlement evidence remains conditional on the owner spec for that prerequisite; the table lists legal edges, not a guarantee that every candidate can traverse every edge.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:107:**[amended v0.1.5]** The authorized actor `coordinator admission policy` acts, for OPERATOR-origin decisions to `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `settlement_capable`, and `revoked`, through exactly one production caller: an **operator decision request** `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions`. **Credential and attribution.** The request is authenticated with the per-actor coordinator operator credential class (`auth.operator_keys`, the class the `/admin` trust-granting surfaces use, which yields an operator actor id) — never the shared single-value `operator_key` — and the appended event's `actor` is `operator:<actor id>` (grammar `^operator:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`). The `settlement_capable` edge, the money-path grant, is **dual-control** exactly as `/admin/hardware-trust/approve` is: the request appends NO event: after steps (1)–(4) below succeed it durably records a pending decision (`pending_decision_id`, grammar `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`; the request's canonical body digest; the evaluated head; `requested_by`; `created_at`; a 24-hour expiry) and answers `model_admission_decision.v1` with the pending values: `previous_admission_state` and `admission_state` both the unchanged current state, `reason_code` the request's reason, `coordinator_event_id` the evaluated head, `accepted_at` the pending record's creation time, `decided_by` the requesting actor, `replayed` false, `pending_decision_id` set, `bound_member` null; a replay of that request answers the same pending record (`replayed: true`); a pending record is consumed by exactly one approval, expires unused, and is invalidated by any event appended for the candidate. `POST /admin/model-admission/decisions/<pending_decision_id>/approve` with request schema `model_admission_decision_approve_request.v1` (exactly `schema`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `pending_decision_id`, `expected_coordinator_event_id`, `idempotency_key`; same grammars) by a DISTINCT operator actor (the same actor is `dual_control_required`; when fewer than two distinct operator actors are configured, the initial `settlement_capable` request itself is refused synchronously with `dual_control_unavailable` and no pending record is created) commits the append under this approval precedence, executed as one unit inside the provider's section: (a) the path and body `pending_decision_id` MUST be equal and the body's `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, and `expected_coordinator_event_id` MUST equal the pending record's stored values, else `invalid_request`; (b) approval idempotency — the approval body is canonicalized and digested under (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical digest answers the committed response (`replayed: true`), a different digest under the same key is `idempotency_conflict`, both before any pending or head check — and because the closed approval body carries nothing but the bound fields and the key, every divergent body under a reused key is a bound-field disagreement already answered by (a), so (a) precedes (b) and `idempotency_conflict` on an approval is defence in depth; (c) pending status — consumed `pending_consumed`, expired `pending_expired`, invalidated or unknown `no_pending_decision`; (d) distinct actor, else `dual_control_required`; (e) the candidate's current head MUST still equal the pending record's evaluated head, else `stale_head` and the record is invalidated; (f) the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions re-evaluated in full; (g) release-generation re-compare and append; an unknown or invalidated id is `no_pending_decision`, an expired one `pending_expired`, a consumed one `pending_consumed`; approvals replay in their own namespace (`pending_decision_id`, `idempotency_key`): an identical-key retry of a committed approval answers the original committed response with `replayed: true`, whatever happened since; a distinct-key approval of a consumed record is `pending_consumed`; two concurrent distinct-key approvals resolve, under the section, as one append and one `pending_consumed`. The other four edges commit on the request. **Bounds.** The request is bounded by payload size and parser work like every SPEC-047-R007 mutation and rate-limited per operator credential and source address; it MUST NOT draw on any per-provider rate window, so a provider cannot exhaust an operator's ability to append a decision for its own candidates. **Request schema** `model_admission_decision_request.v1`, fields exactly `schema`, `provider_id` (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`), `candidate_id` (`^byom_[a-z2-7]{52}$`), `next_state` (one of the five), `reason_code` (`^operator_[a-z0-9_]{2,56}$` — the `operator_` prefix is the operator origin's reserved namespace), `expected_coordinator_event_id` (`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`), and `idempotency_key` (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`); unknown fields are rejected before any state transition. **Precedence**, executed as one unit inside the provider's decision critical section (below): (1) idempotency — the request is canonicalized and keyed by (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `idempotency_key`) (the store's replay index is extended to that triple); an identical canonical request answers with the result it originally produced — the appended event, or the pending decision — whatever the current head, marked `replayed: true`; the same key with a different body fails closed (`idempotency_conflict`); two concurrent first-seen requests with one key resolve as one append plus one replay or one append plus one conflict, never `stale_head`; (2) head compare — `expected_coordinator_event_id` must equal the candidate's current head, else `stale_head`; (3) edge validation against this table from the latest state, else `invalid_transition`; (4) for `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable` only, the SPEC-047-R003 preconditions in their stated order, each with its own code (the other three edges skip this step); (5) under the release read lock (below), the release-generation re-compare and the append as one unit; the appended event records `evaluated_release_generation`. The first failure wins and nothing is appended. **Head and event ids.** `coordinator_event_id` is unique per (`provider_id`, `candidate_id`) — the store's `UNIQUE(provider_id, request_id)` plus the event's own content digest — and the head is the event with the highest append sequence for that candidate, never a content comparison. **Response schema** `model_admission_decision.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `previous_admission_state`, `admission_state`, `reason_code`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, `decided_by` (the actor id), `replayed`, nullable `pending_decision_id`, and — non-null exactly for a committed `settlement_capable` — `bound_member` (`source`, nullable `artifact_id`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`). `model_admission_status.v1` (SPEC-047-R002) keeps its exact field set; its value semantics change in one place, stated in R002. **Transition origins and reason sets are closed and disjoint:** the operator origin appends only the five edges above with `operator_`-prefixed reasons; the offer path appends `offer_submitted` with `provider_offer_submitted`; the withdrawal path appends `withdrawn` with the SPEC-047-R002 withdrawal enum; the synthetic-probe path appends `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, or `revoked` with `synthetic_probe_`-prefixed reasons; the drift path appends `revoked` with exactly one of `runtime_identity_drift`, `catalog_artifact_feed_changed`, `catalog_row_changed`, `catalog_row_ineligible`, `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed`, `receipt_key_unavailable`. Each origin emits only its own REASON set (three target states have two origins); a reason from another origin's set is `invalid_request`. `offer_rejected` is unreachable in v0.1.5: offer validation rejects synchronously (HTTP 4xx, closed code, nothing appended) and no origin appends that edge; the table row stays for a later validator lane, and the R008 rejected-offer cases are stated in terms of synchronous rejection. **Decision critical section.** It is scoped per `provider_id`: every decision and approval, drift event, session-to-candidate binding derivation or mutation (SPEC-047-R003 — whose uniqueness predicate spans all of a provider's candidates), and reload-sweep step for any of the provider's candidates takes that provider's section, and a section is never taken while the provider-registry lock is held (lock order: section, then registry). The provider's section also owns a monotonic **binding generation**, incremented under the section, in the same critical region as the append itself, on every event appended for any of the provider's candidates and on every binding mutation. **Release lock and generation.** The coordinator holds one release read-write lock over ONE immutable release snapshot — the candidate catalog, the compatible-previous catalogs, the artifact feeds and every per-release identity set, the Tier-2 catalog material, and the generation. A reload stages all of them and then takes the WRITE side to swap the whole snapshot and publish its monotonic generation as one act; no part of a release is ever visible before the others. Decisions and approvals take the READ side across the WHOLE evaluation — steps (1)–(5), including every R003 read of catalog rows, identity sets, runtime-source policy, and Tier-2 material — offer-time matching takes it across the match, session identity verification takes it across the verdict, and route-time snapshot creation takes it across the compare-and-insert. **Every append origin takes the provider section**: the offer path, the offer validator, the withdrawal path, the synthetic-probe path, the operator path, and the drift path each acquire the provider's section BEFORE reading candidate state and hold it through the event append, the invalidation of pending decisions for that candidate, the binding-generation increment, and the binding refresh or clear — one linearization point, so no route attempt can observe a candidate set the append has already changed. After publication the R006 sweeps take each provider's section in turn and stamp every surviving `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable` candidate's binding with `validated_release_generation` = the new generation (a candidate the sweep has not yet reached is unroutable, not revoked). BYOM route-time snapshot creation (SPEC-047-R003) takes no provider section: under the release read lock it is an atomic compare-and-insert that re-reads, immediately before the insert, the candidate's head, the session binding and its `bound_coordinator_event_id`, the provider's binding generation captured at evaluation, and requires the binding's `validated_release_generation` to equal the published release generation; any difference fails the attempt closed. **Offer listing.** An operator decides on recorded state, never on a provider's claim: `GET /admin/model-admission/offers?provider_id=<id>` (same credential class; `provider_id` validated by its grammar, any other query parameter rejected) answers `model_admission_offer_list.v1`, exactly `schema`, `generated_at`, `provider_id`, `candidates` — ordered by `candidate_id`, bounded by the per-provider candidate cap — each item exactly `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, `runtime_source` (persisted on the offer event from v0.1.5), `admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `state_observed_at`, `reason_code`, `catalog_match_state`, `catalog_match_reason`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, nullable `catalog_row_model_id`, nullable `catalog_row_model_sha256`, nullable `catalog_release_id`, nullable `catalog_candidate_sha256`, nullable `catalog_signer_key_id`, `catalog_members` (at most 16 tagged members, each exactly `source`, `hash_algorithm`, `hash`, and nullable `artifact_id`, `artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256` — null exactly when `source` is `candidate_row`), `last_event_actor`, and `session` (nullable: `bound`, `bound_coordinator_event_id`, `validated_release_generation`, `verified_member` as a member record or null, `receipt_key_present`, `catalog_release_id`) — the live-session facts R003(iv) will evaluate; the actor of every event (drift included) is readable here, while `model_admission_status.v1` exposes the reason only. A decision request for a candidate with no offer fails closed (`no_offer`). **Errors** on all three endpoints use the existing `{"error":{"code","message"}}` envelope with exactly: `invalid_operator_token` (401), `invalid_request` (400), `no_offer` (404), `stale_head`, `idempotency_conflict`, `invalid_transition`, `catalog_match_required`, `catalog_match_stale`, `catalog_row_not_recommendable`, `catalog_material_unavailable`, `no_verified_session`, `dual_control_required`, `dual_control_unavailable`, `no_pending_decision`, `pending_expired`, `pending_consumed`, `runtime_source_not_allowed` (all 409), and `rate_limited` (429).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:128:**[amended v0.1.3]** For SPEC-047-R001 and SPEC-047-R002, a candidate is **catalog-matched** — the SPEC-046-R003 `identity_state` value `catalog_matched` — when the coordinator verifies that the candidate's locally computed artifact hash equals the `hash` of an artifact whose `verification_status` is `verified`, under that artifact's declared `hash_algorithm`, belonging to a SPEC-023 catalog model key whose `runtime_status` is `listed` or `recommendable`. The match MUST be against a verified artifact of the SPEC-023 §3.7 catalog artifact feed or against the candidate row's own primary `model_sha256`, and MUST bind the algorithm together with the digest. Under SPEC-023 §3.7.4 a `(hash_algorithm, hash)` pair is globally unique within one artifact feed, so a verified feed match resolves to exactly ONE `(model_key, artifact_id)` (a direct candidate-row primary match resolves to the row key with its canonical pair and a null `artifact_id`, since the row defines none — v0.1.5); that resolved model key is the candidate's catalog identity for pricing and tier resolution, a provider-offered `catalog_model_key` is advisory and MUST equal the resolved key or the match fails closed, and a feed in which the pair appears under more than one model key is a SPEC-023 `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure` that MUST produce no catalog match at all. A match against a `candidate` or `blocked` row, against a `declared` or `blocked` artifact, or against a provider-asserted `catalog_model_key`, `served_model_ref`, display name, or runtime-reported label is NOT a catalog match. A catalog match establishes identity only: it is a precondition for `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable`, never a substitute for the SPEC-047-R003 trusted binding, the SPEC-023 tier gate, or the SPEC-022 route-time and receipt preconditions. A `listed` catalog key is catalog-matchable and MUST NOT be treated as priced or settlement-capable. A match against a **non-primary** artifact of a catalog model key — an artifact other than the one named by that key's SPEC-023 `primary_artifact_id`, of any runtime format — is a valid catalog match; **[amended v0.1.4]** under SPEC-010 v1.7 R007 it may advance exactly as a primary match does when the SPEC-010-R007 expected-identity conditions and the SPEC-047-R003 binding hold, and stops at `network_visible_unpriced` otherwise.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:130:**[amended v0.1.5]** **Authority.** The coordinator's offer-time `catalog_match_state` is the ONE authority for a candidate's catalog identity; the SPEC-046-R003 `identity_state` value `catalog_matched` is CLI-local inventory (advisory; the v0.1.3 sentence above describes the coordinator's verification, which this paragraph specifies), and the provider-signed `catalog_model_key` of an offer or withdrawal is a provider claim never read as identity. **Match.** The coordinator performs the catalog match at OFFER time, on the signed `artifact_hashes` of the offer package, resolving every offered `(hash_algorithm, hash)` pair EXACTLY through the two independent paths SPEC-010-R007(b) defines: the **primary-row path** — a `(macprovider.snapshot-manifest.v1, model_sha256)` pair equal to the `model_sha256` of exactly one `listed`/`recommendable` candidate row of the CURRENT admitted release is a row-bound match that needs no artifact feed and carries no feed provenance (a pair equal to more than one row's digest is `primary_row_ambiguous` and matches nothing) — and the **feed path** — any other pair is resolved against the identity set of that release (its release-bound, fresh artifact feed's `verified` artifacts of `listed`/`recommendable` keys), and a release with no usable set (rate-card-bound, feed missing, stale, or integrity-failed) resolves nothing on this path while leaving the primary-row path untouched. A resolved member is admissible for the offer only when the offer's signed `runtime_source` is allowed for it: for an `artifact_feed` member, `runtime_source` ∈ the artifact's `allowed_runtime_sources` (SPEC-023 §3.7.4); for a `candidate_row` member — an `mlx_safetensors` artifact — the sources the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix allows for that format (`mlx_cache`); a member whose sources exclude the offer's is inadmissible for this offer. **Match ordering is fixed:** (1) every offered pair is resolved raw through the two paths; (2) raw resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`) before any admissibility filtering; (3) the runtime-source admissibility filter removes inadmissible members from the admissible member set — they are NOT recorded; (4) the offer is a catalog match when at least one admissible member remains (they all belong to one key by (2)); when (3) leaves none the offer is `unmatched` with `catalog_match_reason` = `runtime_source_not_allowed`. Because one offer carries one signed `runtime_source` and the SPEC-023 §3.7.4 matrix gives `mlx_safetensors` and `gguf` disjoint source sets, one offer records members of ONE runtime format: an `mlx_cache` offer records only the row-bound primary (and any other `mlx_safetensors` member), and a loopback offer records only the members its source allows. **Recorded on the offer event:** `catalog_match_state` ∈ {`catalog_matched`, `unmatched`}; `catalog_match_reason` ∈ {`none`, `no_artifact_match`, `catalog_model_key_disagrees`, `artifact_hashes_span_keys`, `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure`, `primary_row_ambiguous`, `runtime_source_not_allowed`}; for a match, `catalog_model_key` = the RESOLVED row key, the resolved row tuple read from the authenticated candidate catalog — `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256` — the release it was read from as PROVENANCE — `catalog_release_id`, `catalog_candidate_sha256` (the SPEC-023 candidate-catalog body digest; distinct from the SPEC-008 Tier-2 `catalog_body_digest` R003 binds), `catalog_signer_key_id` — and `catalog_members`, every resolved member as a tagged record: `source` ∈ {`candidate_row`, `artifact_feed`}, the pair, and for `artifact_feed` members `artifact_id` plus the provenance of the set it resolved in (`artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, `artifact_candidate_catalog_sha256`), all non-null; for a `candidate_row` member `artifact_id` and the three provenance fields are null (the candidate row defines no artifact id, SPEC-023 §3.2, and none is synthesized). There is no `primary` flag: the six-value obligation of SPEC-047-R003 / SPEC-010-R007(d) is keyed on `source` alone (every `artifact_feed` member carries the six values, the feed's primary entry included). A provider-offered `catalog_model_key` that is non-empty and differs from the resolved key yields NO match (`catalog_model_key_disagrees`); resolved pairs spanning two keys yield NO match (`artifact_hashes_span_keys`); a pair present under two keys or two artifact ids of one identity set is the SPEC-023 `catalog_artifact_feed_integrity_failure` and yields NO match; no resolved pair is `no_artifact_match`. Unmatched offers stand as unmatched offers and MUST store `catalog_model_key` as null. **What a release re-stamp means.** The production catalog renewal re-stamps `version` (a date-embedded release id) and `generated_at` on a schedule while leaving rows and artifact sets untouched, and live sessions survive it as compatible-previous releases (SPEC-010-R004). Catalog identity is therefore anchored on CONTENT — the row tuple (`catalog_model_key`, `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256`) and, per member, `source`, `artifact_id`, and the pair — and the recorded release and feed provenance is evidence of the release the match was evaluated under, never an equality gate: a re-stamp that preserves the row tuple and the member set is a no-op for every recorded match and every admission, and the immutable route-time record (SPEC-047-R003) always carries the provenance of the release the SESSION is actually verified under, which is what settlement re-verifies. A recorded match is never recomputed for an old offer; a decision re-resolves the RECORDED content (R003), and a reload under which that content no longer resolves is drift (R006).
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:134:**SPEC-047-R002 - Offer package schema.** `malibu-cli models offer <candidate> --dry-run --json` MUST produce a local preflight result and MUST NOT submit state. `malibu-cli models offer <candidate> --json` MUST submit a provider-signed offer package only after the operator confirms the candidate, runtime source, served model reference, disclosure class, and non-earning states. The recommended provider workflow is `models discover --json`, `models evaluate <candidate> --json`, `models offer <candidate> --dry-run --json`, and then `models offer <candidate> --json`. Offer dry-run output MUST use a closed JSON envelope with `schema: "model_admission_offer_dry_run.v1"` and MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `would_submit`, `likely_admission_state`, `likely_admission_state_source`, `provider_guidance`, nullable `reason_code`, and `warnings`; `likely_admission_state_source` MUST be `local_default` or `coordinator`; when it is `local_default`, `likely_admission_state` MUST be `local_only`, `not_offered`, or `offerable`; when it is `coordinator`, `likely_admission_state` MUST be one of the SPEC-047-R001 coordinator states; `provider_guidance` MUST reuse the SPEC-046-R003 object shape and closed enums. This is the sole v0.1 dry-run schema; it is not a submission receipt, admission status response, catalog-economics row, or legacy `models_browse.v1` row, and v0.1 decoders MUST reject unknown fields before treating the result as actionable. Offer submission MAY omit the evaluation digest only when the dry-run response explicitly labels the offer as more likely to be rejected or confined to non-earning states. The CLI MUST reserve `models admission status <candidate> --json` for provider status readback and `models admission withdraw <candidate> --json` for provider-initiated withdrawal. `models admission status <candidate> --json` MUST emit a closed JSON envelope with `schema: "model_admission_status.v1"`, `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `admission_state`, `admission_state_source`, nullable `coordinator_event_id`, nullable `state_observed_at`, `provider_guidance`, `allowed_next_states`, and `warnings`. `admission_state_source` MUST be `local_default` or `coordinator`; when it is `local_default`, `admission_state` MUST be `local_only`, `not_offered`, or `offerable`; when it is `coordinator`, `admission_state` MUST be one of the SPEC-047-R001 coordinator states. `provider_guidance` MUST reuse the SPEC-046-R003 object shape and closed enums; for status output, `provider_guidance.next_action` MUST be appropriate to the transition table and `provider_guidance.earning_path_class` MUST be `not_earning_yet_catalog_or_receipt_path_exists`, `no_earning_path_in_v0_1`, `settlement_capable`, or `local_inventory_only`. `allowed_next_states` MUST contain only states allowed by SPEC-047-R001 for coordinator-sourced states and MUST be empty for `local_default` states that have not entered coordinator admission. Revocation, rejection, sanction, withdrawal, and demotion states MUST include a non-null `provider_guidance.transition_reason_code`. The v0.1 offer package MUST be a closed schema; unknown fields MUST be rejected before persistence, state transition, probing, or routing. The v0.1 offer package MUST include schema id, provider id, candidate id, SPEC-046 discovery digest, optional SPEC-046 evaluation digest, runtime source enum, served model reference, catalog match if any, artifact/hash evidence if available, advisory capabilities, fit evidence source, local readiness, requested disclosure class, timestamp, nonce, and provider signature. It MUST NOT include raw prompts, raw completions, endpoint URLs, endpoint origins, hostnames, IP addresses, ports, Unix-domain socket paths, local file paths, raw endpoint credentials, buyer credentials, wallet secrets, or unredacted adapter error bodies. Runtime source and served model reference are identity descriptors only; they MUST NOT be interpreted as network locations for coordinator-side dereference. **[amended v0.1.5]** The `model_admission_status.v1` field set is unchanged, and one value semantic changes: `catalog_model_key` now carries only a coordinator-resolved key (the catalog match of the offer paragraph under SPEC-047-R001) and is null for an unmatched offer, so a provider assertion is never echoed as identity; `provider_guidance.earning_path_class` follows it (`no_earning_path_in_v0_1` for an unmatched offer). Provider-facing visibility of `catalog_match_state`, `catalog_match_reason`, the member set, and the bound member is a later versioned status schema (slice 6), not v1.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:136:`models admission withdraw <candidate> --json` MUST submit a closed coordinator request with `schema: "model_admission_withdraw_request.v1"` and emit the coordinator-derived response with `schema: "model_admission_withdraw.v1"`. The request MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `nonce`, `timestamp`, `reason_code`, `signing_key_id` or `signing_key_digest`, `signature_algorithm`, and `provider_signature`; it MUST NOT include client-provided `previous_admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, or `resulting_admission_state`. `reason_code` MUST be a closed enum; v0.1 values are `provider_requested`, `wrong_model`, `runtime_unavailable`, `identity_mismatch`, `policy_uncertain`, and `other_operator_reason`. The withdrawal signature MUST use the same provider admission identity class as offers, over a canonical domain-separated preimage with domain `macprovider.model_admission.withdraw.v1`, and MUST bind `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `nonce`, `timestamp`, and `reason_code`. Bearer-token authentication may authenticate the transport, but a bearer token alone is never the withdrawal-signing root. Payout keys, wallet private keys, buyer keys, receipt-signing keys, endpoint credentials, and local discovery namespace secrets MUST NOT sign withdrawals or appear in withdrawal payloads. The coordinator MUST reject unknown request fields, stale/unknown/bearer-only/receipt-key-only/payout-key/wallet-key/buyer-key signatures, mismatched provider/candidate/served-model tuples, withdrawals for another provider, replayed nonces, and idempotency-key reuse whose canonical request digest differs from the first request stored for that provider and candidate before appending any event. Exact idempotent retries for the same provider, candidate, idempotency key, and canonical request digest MAY return the original `model_admission_withdraw.v1` response, but MUST NOT append a second state transition or delete local model artifacts. The response MUST include `generated_at`, `cli_version`, `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, nullable `catalog_model_key`, `idempotency_key`, `reason_code`, `previous_admission_state`, `coordinator_event_id`, `accepted_at`, `resulting_admission_state`, `provider_guidance`, and `warnings`; the coordinator MUST derive previous state, event id, acceptance timestamp, and resulting state atomically from durable coordinator state. A later re-entry from `withdrawn` MUST use a fresh provider-signed offer with refreshed evidence digests.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:138:The v0.1 offer package MUST be a closed schema; unknown fields MUST be rejected before persistence, state transition, probing, or routing. The v0.1 offer package MUST include schema id, provider id, candidate id, SPEC-046 discovery digest, optional SPEC-046 evaluation digest, runtime source enum, served model reference, catalog match if any under the SPEC-047-R001 `catalog_matched` definition, artifact/hash evidence if available, advisory capabilities, fit evidence source, local readiness, requested disclosure class, timestamp, nonce, signing key id or digest, provider signature, and signature algorithm. The signing key MUST be the provider's CLI-owned Ed25519 admission identity accepted through SPEC-001/SPEC-026 as the coordinator-authoritative current `provider_admission_public_key` for that `provider_id` at mutation time. Pending or recovery keys qualify for mutating BYOM offers or withdrawals only after the SPEC-026 compare-and-swap or recovery transaction has succeeded and the coordinator now identifies that key as the current admission key. Previous keys are valid only for the rollback/readback compatibility role explicitly allowed by SPEC-026 and MUST NOT authorize mutating BYOM offer or withdrawal requests. The signed payload MUST bind `provider_id`, `candidate_id`, `served_model_ref`, discovery digest, optional evaluation digest, timestamp, nonce/idempotency key, requested disclosure class, and catalog/hash evidence. Bearer-token authentication may be required to authenticate the transport, but a bearer token alone is never the offer-signing root. Payout keys, wallet private keys, buyer keys, receipt-signing keys, endpoint credentials, and local discovery namespace secrets MUST NOT sign BYOM offers or appear in offer payloads. It MUST NOT include raw prompts, raw completions, endpoint URLs, endpoint origins, hostnames, IP addresses, ports, Unix-domain socket paths, local file paths, raw endpoint credentials, buyer credentials, wallet secrets, payout secrets, or unredacted adapter error bodies. Runtime source and served model reference are identity descriptors only; they MUST NOT be interpreted as network locations for coordinator-side dereference.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:140:**SPEC-047-R003 - Settlement boundary.** A model in any state other than `settlement_capable`, including `not_offered`, `offer_submitted`, `offer_rejected`, `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `catalog_priced`, `withdrawn`, or `revoked`, MUST NOT create buyer-final debit, default paid buyer routing, positive provider credit, earnings visibility, payout-ready rows, settlement ledger rows, or "verified" buyer-facing claims. `catalog_priced` MAY show signed rate-card economics only when SPEC-023 and SPEC-044 trust rules are satisfied, but it still MUST NOT create buyer-final debit, default paid buyer routing, positive provider settlement, or settlement ledger rows unless SPEC-022 receipt and route-time verification requirements are also satisfied and the state becomes `settlement_capable`. `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable` require a trusted catalog identity/hash binding: the coordinator MUST bind the candidate to a trusted signed catalog row by catalog identity, exact catalog body digest, signing key identity, `catalog_model_key`, expected `model_hash`/algorithm, and route-time snapshot evidence under SPEC-010 and SPEC-022. **[amended v0.1.3]** That trusted binding MAY reference an artifact of the SPEC-023 §3.7 catalog artifact feed instead of the candidate row's single `model_sha256`. When it does, the recorded binding MUST include the artifact feed's exact body digest (`artifact_feed_sha256`), the artifact `hash`, and the artifact `hash_algorithm`, in addition to the candidate catalog's own exact body digest, signing key identity, and `catalog_model_key`; the artifact feed MUST be release-bound to that candidate catalog under SPEC-023 §3.7.4, and the artifact MUST carry `verification_status: "verified"`. The artifact feed's authenticated signer identity MUST be recorded alongside them as `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`; under SPEC-023 §3.7.2 (as scoped in v0.10.2) that `key_id` MUST equal the authenticated candidate-feed signer of that release — and, wherever the consumer holds the authenticated `release.json`, its artifact-feed `signer_key_id` — so the artifact signer is not inherited from the candidate signer by assumption but recorded after that equality check succeeds. **[amended v0.1.3]** Artifact evidence MUST be captured in the IMMUTABLE route-time record, never only in mutable admission state. For a request attempt whose binding references a §3.7 artifact, the SPEC-022 route-time verification snapshot MUST carry — directly, or in a separate immutable artifact-binding record that the snapshot references by digest and that is itself immutable once written — all six of `artifact_feed_sha256`, `artifact_id`, the artifact `hash`, the artifact `hash_algorithm`, `artifact_feed_signer_key_id`, and the exact candidate-catalog body digest that feed is release-bound to. **That extension is a SPEC-047-owned OPTIONAL record. SPEC-022's minimum route-time snapshot field list is unchanged and SPEC-022 is NOT amended by this revision:** SPEC-022 states those fields as a minimum the snapshot "contains at least", which an owner spec may extend, and the settlement-capable receipt profile already binds the snapshot by digest, so the extension travels under the binding SPEC-022 already requires. At settlement the coordinator MUST re-verify that evidence against the snapshot and MUST fail closed — no buyer-final debit, no default paid routing, no positive provider settlement, no settlement ledger row — when the artifact evidence is **missing** (an artifact-derived binding whose snapshot carries none of the six values, or whose referenced record does not resolve to the digest the snapshot recorded), **changed** (any of the six values differs from the snapshot's), **cross-release** (an `artifact_feed_sha256` or candidate-catalog body digest belonging to a different release than the snapshot recorded, even when the artifact `hash` still matches), or **wrong-signer** (an `artifact_feed_signer_key_id` differing from the snapshot's, including a cryptographically valid signature by a different concurrently trusted key). Fail-closed here is a refusal to settle and never a repair: settlement MUST NOT consult a current artifact feed, a current `release.json`, or a current keyring to reconstruct evidence a snapshot does not carry. **[amended v0.1.4]** Which artifacts of that catalog model key may be a settlement identity is SPEC-010's decision: under SPEC-010 v1.7 **R007** any `verified` artifact of the release-bound artifact feed for a `listed`/`recommendable` key is a member of the key's identity set — the primary member is the row's own `model_sha256` (SPEC-010-R001), and `macprovider.gguf-file.v1` is a canonical SPEC-010-R002 wire pair — and a binding MAY name any member whose `(hash_algorithm, hash)` pair the provider reports exactly (recomputed over the bytes it holds, never adopted from a runtime report). The model key of that binding is the one the globally unique SPEC-023 §3.7.4 pair resolves to; a provider-asserted `catalog_model_key` that disagrees with the resolved key MUST fail the binding closed rather than select a price. Every binding that references an artifact-feed entry — the feed's primary entry included; only a primary identity bound directly through the signed candidate row is exempt — MUST carry the six values above in the immutable route-time record, and settlement MUST re-verify them fail-closed as stated. Which artifacts are excluded from being an expected identity, and what a failed artifact-derived verification leaves standing, is stated once in SPEC-010-R007(b) and cited here, not restated (the v0.1.3 primary-only text is superseded). When SPEC-010-R007(b) excludes a feed or an artifact from being an expected identity, artifact-derived binding fails closed and MUST NOT be substituted by a provider-asserted or runtime-reported artifact identity. A release-manifest digest MAY be recorded as additional provenance only when its owner spec defines the field, but it is never an alternative to the exact catalog body digest required for settlement-capable route snapshots. Provider-asserted `catalog_model_key`, `served_model_ref`, display name, runtime-reported model name, or local artifact label is advisory only and is never sufficient for catalog economics or settlement capability. `settlement_capable` is the only v0.1 BYOM admission state that may participate in buyer-final debit, default paid buyer routing, positive provider settlement, and payout-ready ledger behavior, and only for request attempts whose route-time snapshot and receipt verification satisfy SPEC-022.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:142:**[amended v0.1.5]** An operator decision (SPEC-047-R001) to `catalog_priced` or `settlement_capable` MUST fail closed — appending nothing, answering with the clause's code — unless, evaluated inside the provider's decision critical section (SPEC-047-R001; one section per `provider_id`) at decision time (and, for the dual-control `settlement_capable` edge, again at approval time): (i) the candidate's latest offer event carries `catalog_match_state` = `catalog_matched` (`catalog_match_required` otherwise), and every recorded member still resolves in the CURRENT release: a `candidate_row` member's row tuple (`catalog_model_key`, `catalog_row_model_id`, `catalog_row_model_sha256`) is present in the current candidate catalog, and an `artifact_feed` member resolves in the current identity set to the same (`catalog_model_key`, `artifact_id`, pair) — provenance MAY differ (a re-stamp) and the decision records the CURRENT provenance; any member that no longer resolves is `catalog_match_stale` (a content change requires a fresh offer; evidence is never repaired); (ii) that row's `runtime_status` is `recommendable` in the current candidate catalog (`catalog_row_not_recommendable` for a `listed`, `candidate`, or `blocked` row — a removed row already failed (i); SPEC-023 AC-CAT-7(iii)), and every recorded member still allows the recorded `runtime_source` (`runtime_source_not_allowed` otherwise); the coordinator stamps the row's status on every bound session as `catalog_row_status` and refreshes it in the R006(c) sweep, and the buyer re-reads it at route time as defence in depth (redundant by construction, since a change is also a linearized revocation); (iii) trusted Tier-2 catalog material exists for that row (`catalog_material_unavailable` otherwise), and the decision event binds `catalog_id`, `catalog_body_digest`, `catalog_signature_key_id`, `catalog_signature_pubkey_fingerprint` from it and `catalog_model_key` = the resolved key — that material is proof of the ROW binding (catalog identity, body digest, signer, and the row's own `model_sha256`, the primary member) and the pricing key; for an `artifact_feed` member it is never proof of the member's hash, which is proven only by the member's six values (SPEC-010-R004 v1.8, R007(d)); the binding is that composite and an implementation MUST NOT read the row material's digest as the member's expected hash; (iv) for `settlement_capable` only, the provider's live session — the registry keeps exactly ONE active session per provider id; a new hello replaces the previous session and re-derives its binding — MUST be bound to this candidate (below), admitted on the current release or on a retained compatible-previous release whose catalog carries the same row tuple, with a SPEC-010 identity verdict that is `hash_verified` and pinned (SPEC-010-R007(b)/(c) session authority) for a pair that is one of the recorded members admissible for the recorded `runtime_source` (the serving path a session presents is that source; a session can present only `mlx_cache` and only an `mlx_safetensors` member can bind — **[amended v0.1.10]** a loopback source never binds, per the loopback settlement bar below), resolved in the identity set of the session's OWN admitted release (SPEC-010-R004 v1.8: the coordinator retains the identity set of each compatible-previous release it retains), and with its SPEC-022 receipt key present; no such session is `no_verified_session`. The decision event then binds THAT member as the settlement identity: `expected_catalog_model_hash` / `_algorithm` = its pair and, for an `artifact_feed` member, the six SPEC-047-R003 values of the session's binding (the provenance of the release the session resolved in); a `candidate_row` member binds the row directly and carries none. A `catalog_priced` decision binds the key and the member set, not a served member. **Session-to-candidate binding** is coordinator-derived, never provider-asserted: at hello (initial or replacement) and whenever an event is appended for a provider's candidate, the coordinator binds the session to the candidate whose latest non-terminal event (`offer_submitted` through `settlement_capable`) is `catalog_matched` on the row whose `model_id` the session serves; zero candidates bind nothing (an unmatched candidate never binds, so the non-BYOM session path applies) and two or more bind nothing, the coordinator logs `ambiguous_candidates`, and R006(a) then treats the affected `catalog_priced`/`settlement_capable` candidates as identity drift (the session no longer verifies for a bound candidate). The binding is `candidate_id`, `catalog_model_key`, the candidate's current `coordinator_event_id`, and `catalog_row_status`; it is refreshed on every event appended for that candidate (a revocation refreshes it to the terminal event and thereby clears routability), cleared on withdrawal, model change, and disconnect, and re-derived at the next hello; every binding mutation takes the provider's section. Buyer default routing and settlement MUST require a session binding whose `coordinator_event_id` equals the candidate's latest event and whose state is `settlement_capable`, MUST compare the session's verified pair (and `artifact_id`, for a feed member) to the decision's bound member by CONTENT, and MUST create and persist the BYOM route-time snapshot by the compare-and-insert of SPEC-047-R001 (re-reading head, binding, and release generation immediately before the insert), recording the session's CURRENT binding provenance; served-model-name or asserted-key lookups are never a fallback.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:144:**[amended v0.1.10] Loopback settlement bar (#1694).** A candidate whose recorded `runtime_source` is a SPEC-046-R002 loopback adapter (`ollama_loopback`, `lmstudio_loopback`, `llamacpp_loopback`, `openai_compatible_loopback`) MUST NOT reach `settlement_capable`, and no session whose hello-time `runtime_source` is a loopback adapter binds for settlement under (iv), until a trusted usage source exists for that path. The external runtime is an operator-controlled process whose reported `usage` the CLI relays unchanged, so its token counts are provider-only usage under SPEC-015 §N.6; the delivered-bytes and prompt-bound clamps (SPEC-005) are ceilings, not a trust source. A decision request or approval for such a candidate or session answers `no_verified_session` (no new reason code). This bar is independent of the SPEC-010-R007(e) runtime path: implementing that path does NOT lift it, and neither does the provider-signed `runtime_source` value, which is a provider assertion. Lifting it requires a later amendment of this requirement naming a coordinator-recorded trust binding for the path (for example SPEC-042 pool policy, issue #1690) and the trusted usage source it relies on. **Defence in depth,** each redundant by construction while the admission bar holds: (a) buyer default routing and settlement MUST NOT treat a `settlement_capable` decision as settlement-eligible when the decision's recorded `runtime_source` or the serving session's hello-time `runtime_source` is a loopback adapter, whatever member it bound; (b) settlement-attempt recording MUST take the serving session's hello-time `runtime_source` and MUST NOT record an attempt served by a loopback-source session with `usage_source` = `coordinator_observed`; such an attempt is recorded `byte_estimated`, which carries zero billable usage and is never settlement-capable (SPEC-015 §N.6). Native catalog sessions (`mlx_cache`, or a hello that reports no source) are unchanged.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:146:**SPEC-047-R004 - Pricing and economics.** Provider-proposed prices, local benchmark estimates, runtime-reported model names, and demand labels are advisory until converted into a signed MacProvider rate-card entry or a later billing-owner spec defines another trusted price source. The coordinator and Malibu MUST NOT display provider payout rates, expected earnings, higher-paying labels, or catalog economics for `not_offered`, `offer_submitted`, `offer_rejected`, `sandbox_probe_only`, `network_visible_unpriced`, `network_admitted_unsettled`, `withdrawn`, or `revoked` states. `catalog_priced` MAY display signed catalog economics under SPEC-044 while still hiding earning-eligible or settlement-ready claims until the state becomes `settlement_capable`. If an offer has no trusted price, buyer-visible surfaces MAY label it only as unpriced or experimental when explicitly opted in; provider-facing surfaces MUST state that the model is not earning-eligible. Provider-facing status MUST distinguish "not earning-eligible yet; catalog/receipt path exists" from "no earning path exists in this release because the model lacks a trusted price-conversion/catalog path." For `settlement_capable`, `provider_guidance.earning_path_class` expresses eligibility only: the provider/candidate pair may participate in positive settlement for a request attempt that later satisfies every SPEC-022 route-time snapshot and verified-receipt predicate. Provider-facing human output MUST use **Eligible to earn on qualifying settled requests** and MUST NOT imply that the candidate is prepared, serving, receiving demand, currently producing income, or guaranteed to receive or settle a request. A catalog-only SPEC-044 row with no candidate/guidance/binding cannot consume this per-candidate admission state or construct any independent positive economics case.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:148:**SPEC-047-R005 - Buyer visibility and routing.** Default public buyer `/v1/models` and default buyer routing MUST include only models that are allowed by SPEC-006 and the active routing policy. Non-settlement BYOM states MUST be hidden from default paid routing. Experimental or unpriced visibility, if enabled, MUST require an explicit account, request, or operator policy opt-in and MUST return disclosure fields that distinguish provider-reported identity from catalog-verified identity. A sole-provider or low-supply condition MUST NOT relax catalog, admission, route-time snapshot, or settlement requirements.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:150:**SPEC-047-R006 - Drift, revocation, and withdrawal.** Providers MUST be able to withdraw an offered candidate through a CLI-owned command. The coordinator MUST revoke or demote an admitted candidate when required identity, artifact/hash, runtime health, hardware fit, policy, or receipt preconditions become stale, mismatched, expired, or unavailable. A provider heartbeat, warm-swap event, loaded-model hash, adapter identity, or runtime source that no longer matches the admitted route-time predicate MUST fail closed for buyer routing and settlement. Revocation MUST be visible in provider-facing status with a reason code and MUST NOT require deleting local model artifacts.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:152:**[amended v0.1.5]** Drift is a CONTENT change, never a provenance-only change: a release re-stamp that preserves the row tuple and the member set appends nothing. The following drift sources MUST be live in production, each a coordinator-actor event under the provider's decision critical section (SPEC-047-R001) and visible in status readback with its reason code: (a) a hello — initial or replacement, evaluated inside the section BEFORE the incoming session's binding is published, against the candidate the prior binding named or, when no prior binding exists (after a disconnect or a coordinator restart), against the candidate the newly derived binding names — a heartbeat, or a refresh under which the session of a `catalog_priced` or `settlement_capable` candidate serves another model id or is no longer `hash_verified` for a recorded member (another identity, the primary pair for a member-pinned session, a hash-less or unnamed-algorithm report, an unverifiable pair, an ambiguous-candidates derivation) MUST append `revoked` with `runtime_identity_drift` (one code for the served-model-id and identity-verdict predicates; the existing model-id drift path emits it but looks candidates up by `served_model_ref` — it is replaced by the binding); (b) after every artifact-feed reload, every recorded `artifact_feed` member of every `catalog_priced` / `settlement_capable` candidate MUST be re-resolved in the new current identity set, and a member that no longer resolves to the same (`catalog_model_key`, `artifact_id`, pair) MUST append `revoked` with `catalog_artifact_feed_changed` — a changed feed digest or signer alone is not drift; a reload that leaves the current release with no usable set revokes every candidate that has an `artifact_feed` member; a candidate whose recorded members are all `candidate_row` is unaffected by feed state; (c) after every candidate-catalog reload (and whenever the admitted catalog becomes unavailable), every `catalog_priced` / `settlement_capable` candidate MUST be re-evaluated against SPEC-047-R003 (i)–(iii) under the new release snapshot (the Tier-2 material is part of that atomic snapshot, SPEC-047-R001), and a candidate whose bound `catalog_id`, `catalog_body_digest`, or `catalog_signature_key_id` no longer equals the current material MUST append `revoked` with `catalog_row_changed` — and its recorded row tuple MUST be re-read from the new catalog: a row that no longer exists or whose key, `model_id`, or `model_sha256` changed MUST append `revoked` with `catalog_row_changed`, and a row whose `runtime_status` is no longer `recommendable` (unchanged digest) MUST append `revoked` with `catalog_row_ineligible`, a recorded member whose `allowed_runtime_sources` no longer include the recorded `runtime_source` MUST append `revoked` with `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed`, and every bound session's `catalog_row_status` and `validated_release_generation` are refreshed; (d) a hello (initial or replacement, evaluated as in (a)) or heartbeat under which the session of a `settlement_capable` candidate no longer presents its SPEC-022 receipt key MUST append `revoked` with `receipt_key_unavailable`; a DISCONNECT is not a durable transition — it clears the session binding, which alone makes the candidate unroutable until the next hello rebinds and is evaluated under (a) and (d). Revocation is append-only; re-entry is a fresh signed offer through the R001 table.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:154:**SPEC-047-R007 - Abuse and privacy controls.** Offer submission and withdrawal MUST be authenticated as the provider, signed with the SPEC-047-R002 current provider admission identity, rate-limited per provider identity, bounded by payload size and parser work, replay-protected by nonce or idempotency key, and audited. The coordinator MUST verify that the signing public key is the current coordinator-authoritative `provider_admission_public_key` for the `provider_id` at mutation time; pending or recovery keys can authorize BYOM mutation only after the SPEC-026 transaction has made them current, and previous keys remain limited to SPEC-026 rollback/readback compatibility. Stale, unknown, bearer-only, receipt-key-only, payout-key, wallet-key, buyer-key, pending-key-not-current, recovery-key-not-current, or previous-key-mutating signatures MUST fail closed. The coordinator MUST reject offers containing endpoint URLs, endpoint origins, hostnames, IP addresses, port values, Unix-domain socket paths, public/LAN/loopback/private/link-local/multicast address material, redirect targets, encoded network locations, secret-bearing fields, raw local absolute paths, HTML/script-bearing display names, control characters, ambiguous Unicode identifiers, or model identifiers that cannot be normalized under the chosen identity class. Offer state MUST be sanction-aware: a provider under a route, trust, payout, or registration sanction MUST NOT use BYOM admission to bypass that sanction.
specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:156:**SPEC-047-R008 - Release evidence.** Promotion beyond draft MUST include automated tests for offer dry-run non-submission, provider signature verification, replay rejection, closed-schema unknown-field rejection, endpoint/origin/socket/path rejection including loopback, localhost, IPv6 loopback, encoded IP, redirect, Unix-socket, and local-path variants, state-machine transition validity including withdrawn/revoked re-offer freshness and, for rejection, that a synchronously rejected offer (HTTP 4xx, closed code) appends nothing and a fresh compliant offer is then accepted, `models admission status` presentation of provider-facing state meaning, next action, and earning-path disclosure, synthetic probes using the provider wire protocol rather than coordinator dereference, settlement-boundary enforcement, default buyer invisibility for non-settlement states, explicit experimental disclosure if implemented, pricing trust nullability, revocation on drift, withdrawal, sanction interaction, payload redaction, parser/resource bounds, and SPEC-044 economics gating. Localization and accessibility fixtures for `settlement_capable` MUST preserve **Eligible to earn on qualifying settled requests** as conditional eligibility and reject current-income, current-serving, guaranteed-demand, and guaranteed-settlement meanings. Fixtures for coordinator-backed `not_offered` MUST preserve the exact English source meaning **Coordinator reports no active network offer for this model.** and MUST distinguish it from SPEC-046 `local_default:not_offered`, which cannot assert offer history. Production promotion MUST include a signed journey result covering one rejected opaque endpoint, one sandbox-probe-only offer, one network-visible unpriced offer, one catalog-matched offer that is not yet settlement-capable, one novel non-catalog offer whose status says no earning path exists in v0.1, one synchronously rejected offer followed by a fresh accepted offer, one revoked drift case, one withdrawn re-entry requiring fresh evidence, and one settlement-capable catalog-verified case. **[amended v0.1.5]** Promotion MUST additionally include automated tests for: per-actor operator authentication (the shared `operator_key` is refused), the closed decision request/response grammars (unknown field, bad state, bad reason including every reserved internal reason and every withdrawal-enum value, bad idempotency key, malformed `expected_coordinator_event_id`), dual control on `settlement_capable` (same actor cannot approve; approval re-evaluates preconditions); precedence (`stale_head` before `invalid_transition` before precondition codes; identical replay answers the original event after the head advanced; divergent reuse fails; two concurrent first-seen requests with one key); a decision for a candidate with no offer; offer-time matching through both paths (row-bound primary with no usable set; feed-path member; an `mlx_cache` offer carrying a primary pair and a GGUF pair of one key records the primary member only, and the same pairs under a loopback source record the GGUF member only; raw pairs spanning keys rejected before admissibility filtering; a disagreeing asserted key; an integrity-failed set; an ambiguous primary row) with `catalog_match_reason` recorded and listed; the `listed` ceiling at decision time (`catalog_row_not_recommendable`); a release RE-STAMP (new release id, digest, and feed signature, unchanged rows and members) that changes NOTHING — no revocation, decisions still commit, sessions on the previous release still settle; a content change per field (key, `model_id`, `model_sha256` each independently, a member removed from the set, a feed dropped) that revokes with the matching code; the session-binding lifecycle (derive at hello and at offer; unmatched and ambiguous candidates bind nothing; refresh on decision; revocation refresh clears routability; clear on withdrawal/model change/disconnect; route-time event-id equality and bound-member content equality); `settlement_capable` with no bound verified session and with the single bound verified session, a replacing hello re-deriving the binding, and a session on a retained compatible-previous release verified in its own release's identity set; hello-time drift (initial hello after disconnect, replacement hello) lacking the receipt key or failing the pinned-member predicate revoking before the new session is observable as bound; decision-vs-revocation, decision-vs-reload (generation change fails the decision closed), decision-vs-hello/disconnect/model-change/offer-rebinding interleavings under the section; route-snapshot compare-and-insert against revocation, withdrawal, demotion, identity drift, row change, and reload (the attempt fails closed or the immutable snapshot stands); the reload sweeps over both `catalog_priced` and `settlement_capable`; the offer-listing schema, ordering, cap, member bound, session facts, and provider isolation; operator rate limiting independent of the target provider's window; a value-semantics test that an unmatched offer yields `catalog_model_key: null` and `earning_path_class: no_earning_path_in_v0_1` while the `model_admission_status.v1` field set is unchanged; that every drift event records the actor and the reason, the reason readable through `models admission status` and the actor through the operator listing; `runtime_source_not_allowed` at match and decision time and `catalog_runtime_source_disallowed` on reload; the dual-control protocol (pending record; request replay answers the pending record; fewer than two configured actors → synchronous `dual_control_unavailable`, no record; approval by the same actor refused; approval after a head change refused and the record invalidated; expiry; identical-key approval retry answers the committed response; distinct-key double approval → one append + `pending_consumed`); a Tier-2 material change on reload revoking a surviving candidate (`catalog_row_changed`); a reader that observes the Tier-2 material, the catalog, and the identity sets of one and the same generation only (a staged reload is invisible until published); an approval whose path and body ids or bound fields disagree (`invalid_request`), a divergent approval body under a reused key (`invalid_request` under (a): every divergence of the closed body is a bound-field disagreement; the `idempotency_conflict` branch of (b) stays as defence in depth), and the pending-response values of the initial `settlement_capable` request; an offer appended for candidate B while a route attempt for candidate A of the same row is in flight — the attempt fails closed on the binding generation and an offer whose only resolvable member is disallowed for its `runtime_source` recorded as `unmatched` / `runtime_source_not_allowed` with an empty member set; a reader that starts a decision before a reload's write lock and one that starts after (the first appends under the old generation and is revalidated or revoked by the sweep before any route attempt succeeds; the second sees only the fully installed release); a route attempt between publication and the sweep reaching the candidate fails closed; and a second candidate for the same row appended while the first is routable — the binding generation makes the in-flight route attempt fail closed.

specs/SPEC-047-network-model-admission.md:192:The route from local candidate to earning is intentionally multi-step: discovered locally, evaluated locally, offered to the network, admitted for limited network state, catalog-priced when a trusted rate-card source exists, and settlement-capable only when route-time verification and receipts satisfy SPEC-022. This makes model supply broad without letting arbitrary local endpoints mint provider credit.

specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:78:- **v0.2.2 (2026-06-27, r2 absorption):** Absorbs the seven round-2 findings. AC-46 and §10d.0.1 now use a single unknown-hash contract: every v0.2 response includes `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed`, with `null` when no provider hash is known and lowercase 64-character SHA-256 hex when known; AC-25a release evidence captures the value while Cline remains required to ignore it. `prompt_echo_blocked` is removed from the buyer-visible v0.2 error-envelope table and remains only an internal log code for plain-content fallback. Mechanical edits update the live hash-routing citation, add AC-50 through AC-55 for aggregate request caps and linear validation, explain §10d's deliverable-numbered subsections, note why §3.8 physically precedes locked §3.7, and document that `invalid_tools` is inherited from SPEC-001 / SPEC-002 request validation.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:82:- Minimal v0.2 mitigations replace the deferred registry for this narrow Cline drop-in slice: exact-verbatim prompt-echo blocking, tightened final-close settlement gating, and passive `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed` observation.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:83:- Streaming final-close is now protocol-complete: accumulated arguments, `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, normal transport terminal marker, and no post-open disconnect/error are all required before provider-positive settlement.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:89:- **v0.2.1 (2026-06-27, r1 absorption):** Absorbs the 22 round-1 audit findings. **Load-bearing amendment:** the "§10c v0.1.3-locked clause re v0.2 model-hash registry is amended in v0.2.0/v0.2.1 to defer registry to v0.3." Rationale: narrow v0.2 scope (Cline drop-in) makes registry curation strategically premature, and a binary-baked stub registry does not add real security value without curation governance. Precedent: locked invariants are NOT immutable, but they require an explicit named amendment with rationale; this is the first such amendment in SPEC-018. In lieu of the registry, v0.2.1 adds the §3.9 minimal prompt-echo guard, tightens §8.4.2 final-close, and adds AC-46 passive model-hash binding observation. **Second explicit lock amendment:** the duplicate v0.2 additive §3.7 heading is renumbered to §3.8 so locked §3.7 "Adding a new family" remains unambiguous. **Money path:** final-close failure now includes missing terminal argument state, missing `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, missing transport completion marker, or any provider disconnect/timeout/relay/auth/truncation after incremental-open; all such paths are `FaultBreakerQualifying`, zero provider-positive credits, no receipt, and no sticky-route success write. **Streaming safety:** terminal error SSE events MUST NOT carry `finish_reason:"tool_calls"` and SDKs are expected to raise/failed-stream rather than deliver dispatchable tool calls. **Mechanics:** canonicalizes missing `tool_call_id` to `invalid_tool_call_id`, scopes AC-14/AC-8/AC-9 to v0.1.x, adds §10d reader/Cline rationale notes, updates v0.2 code citations, makes renderer fixtures implementation-verifiable against upstream Qwen3/Llama-3.3 chat templates, replaces placeholder SSE IDs, splits AC-25, instruments AC-44, adds `X-MacProvider-Streaming-Mode`, thickens v0.2 error envelopes, adds aggregate request/streaming budgets, and clarifies buyer-fabricated history as prompt data rather than provider provenance.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:94:- §8.4 gains a v0.2 split for token-incremental streaming: incremental-open permits buyer-visible streaming; final-close gates money-path settlement; no withdrawal to plain content is allowed after a tool-call delta is emitted.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:98:- v0.3 candidates are explicitly deferred: model-hash registry, prompt-echo guard, and structured `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call` exposure.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:100:- **v0.2.0 (2026-06-27, narrow Cline-drop-in draft):** Adds the minimum surface required for "point Cline at macprovider and complete a real multi-turn coding session" on top of locked v0.1.5. **Multi-turn:** AC-14 is closed by requiring the phase3 provider to accept `role:"tool"` messages and assistant-history `tool_calls[]`, preserve `tool_call_id` / `tool_calls` through request parsing, validate the in-request graph, and render prior assistant tool calls plus tool results into the selected model family's native chat-template markup. Current rejection paths are `phase3-binary/Sources/macprovider-cli/ModelRuntime.swift:909`, call sites `:353` and `:403`, with exact rejects at `:924` and `:931`; `ChatCompletionRequest.swift:194` / `:202` already validate the structured shapes but `ChatMessage` at `:175` must preserve fields that are currently lost before `request.messages.map { $0.mlxMessage }` at `ModelRuntime.swift:374`, `:428`, and `:513`. **Family renderer:** adds a v0.2 tool prompt-template profile for the input render direction, separate from §3.1 output parser-family selection; v0.2 keys it by modelID-match per §3.2, while the v0.3 registry candidate will move it to verified `model_hash`. **Request caps:** `role:"tool"` content is capped at 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes per message with HTTP 413 `tool_result_too_large`; assistant-history `function.arguments` is capped at 1 MiB with HTTP 413 `tool_call_arguments_too_large`. **Receipts:** no schema change; `PromptCanonicalizer.swift:5` already canonicalizes `messages`, including `tool_call_id` and `tool_calls` at `:31`, but v0.2 requires regression tests proving `prompt_hash` changes when those fields change. **Streaming:** promotes token-incremental OpenAI-style `tool_calls[].function.arguments` deltas, keyed by `index`, with first delta carrying `id` / `type` / `function.name` and later deltas carrying argument fragments. §8.4 is extended with incremental-open, final-close, and no-withdrawal rules; the current coordinator validator at `phase4-coordinator/internal/buyer/server.go:2674` is incompatible with OpenAI incremental fragments and must be replaced for both `forwardWSStreaming` (`server.go:2103`, buyer byte write at `:2149`) and `forwardStreaming` (`server.go:2279`). **Money path:** buyer-visible streaming commit happens at incremental-open, while provider-positive settlement commits only after final-close; mid-stream cap-cross or final-close failure remains `FaultBreakerQualifying` with zero provider-positive credits through existing `phase4-coordinator/internal/buyer/billing_recorder.go:176` and `phase4-coordinator/internal/billing/formula.go:112`. **Argument caps:** replaces the v0.1.5 response-side 256 KiB DoS bound with public v0.2 constants `1_048_576` bytes per call, `2_097_152` bytes per response, and depth `32`, identical at parser and coordinator. **Forward compatibility:** extends AC-23 with AC-23s streaming regression using `openai==2.44.0`, and adds §10c cap invariants that future v0.2.x may raise but not lower the caps or change the inclusive UTF-8 unescaped counting domain. **Deferred:** model-hash registry, prompt-echo guard, and structured `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call` remain v0.3 candidates only; v0.2 may use internal failure reasons for logs and terminating SSE error frames but does not expose the v0.3 usage schema.

Reworked to capture vN.M responses and parse with v0.1.2 parser. **H-2 absorbed:** §1 named "Claude Code, Cursor" as OpenAI-shape frameworks; both speak proprietary / Anthropic wires. Removed across §1, §1.1, §10a #1, §11 Q1 + replaced with accurate 5-framework list. **H-3 absorbed:** §3.6 mixed-sentinel rule was a DoS vector — any prompt containing `<|python_tag|>` would suppress legitimate Qwen tool calls. Dropped §3.6 mixed-sentinel pre-detection, AC-22, IMPL delta #2 (mixed-sentinel). §3.2 modelID-match-required closes the cross-family bypass on its own. **5 MEDIUMs absorbed:** M-1 JSON depth/byte cap in §8.4 + §3.4 (DoS via 100k-deep nested objects); M-2 operator-override loophole in §10a #2 replaced with buyer-consent header + mandatory response field; M-3 §6 pass-through MUST gets AC-24 verification at WS frame layer; M-4 §10c id value format protection (call_ prefix); M-5 §2.3 sorted-keys recursive at every depth (SPEC-015 receipts binding). **Narrative 5 MINORs absorbed:** m-1 change log gets buyer-visible bullets at top; m-2 Status line gets descriptive parenthetical; m-3 §3.2 rationale gains "modelID is self-declared; model_hash is verified" sentence; m-4 §3 "family-family priority" typo fixed; m-5 §1 IMPL-prompt scaffolding moved to new §1.2. **Critic Qs pinned:** AC-16b "passes" verb (Q-1); `null` vs missing arguments distinction (Q-2); §3.6 dropped per H-3 (Q-3). **Narrative Q absorbed:** §10a #2 v0.2-MUST clause relocated to §10c as v0.1.3-locked v0.2 invariant (Narrative Q-1).
