specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:220:- JSON object arguments decoded from a structured object MUST be serialized with **keys sorted recursively at every depth** (nested objects' keys are also sorted), no insignificant whitespace, and without escaping `/`. The recursive sort is required for SPEC-015 v0.3 receipt canonical-output binding (per AC-17): a non-recursive sort would produce a wire bytestring that disagrees with the receipt's canonicalized hash for any tool call with nested-object arguments.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:398:1. **Visible content:** `choices[0].message.content` is the concatenation of completed `final` channel body token spans only, except for the narrow visible-final truncation case defined in rule 5. `analysis` channel bodies and all non-tool `commentary` channel bodies MUST NOT appear in `message.content`, streaming `delta.content`, logs intended as buyer-visible response data, receipts, or usage-visible content accounting. A Harmony response with tool calls and no final-channel content uses the existing OpenAI tool-call content behavior (`message.content = null`).
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:402:5. **Token accounting and visible-final truncation:** For Harmony responses, buyer API `usage.completion_tokens` MUST count only token IDs in `final` channel body spans that become buyer-visible assistant content. Structural Harmony tokens, `analysis` body tokens, `commentary` body tokens, tool-call JSON body tokens, constrain/header tokens, and call/end/return markers MUST NOT contribute to API `completion_tokens`. This buyer-visible usage rule does not redefine receipt or settlement accounting: receipt/settlement `tokens_out` remains the actual generated output token count per SPEC-015 and the settlement profile. A Harmony completion that emits only tool calls and no final-channel content therefore has API `completion_tokens = 0` while receipt/settlement `tokens_out` records the generated Harmony tokens. If generation ends by `length` or request stop while already inside a `final` channel body, the implementation MAY expose the filtered final-body prefix generated so far and count only those emitted final-body tokens in API usage; this exception does not apply to hidden `analysis`, `commentary`, role/header, constrain, or function-call JSON spans, which remain fail-closed as `malformed_tool_call_final_json` when structurally incomplete. If a request stop is observed inside the visible final-body prefix, later Harmony frames and tool calls MUST be suppressed.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:436:The provider MAY then emit a usage chunk with `choices = []` and MUST end the stream with `[DONE]`.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:538:Malformed or oversized pre-commit tool-call deltas — including `{"choices":[{"delta":{"tool_calls":[{}]}}]}` (empty tool-call object), `{"function":{"arguments":"[]"}}` (arguments decodes to non-object), and `{"function":{"arguments":"<256-KiB-of-nested-objects>"}}` (exceeds size or depth cap) — MUST NOT commit the response and MUST NOT settle provider-positive usage. This closes the Security H-1 commit-on-bogus-delta path AND the v0.1.3 Critic M-1 commit-validator DoS path (an adversarial provider sending arbitrarily deep nested JSON to exhaust the coordinator commit-signal goroutine's stack).
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:557:Passing incremental-open permits buyer-visible streaming commit: the provider may start emitting OpenAI-style `tool_calls[].function.arguments` fragments keyed by `index`. It does **not** commit provider-positive settlement.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:563:At end-of-stream, before provider-positive settlement is finalized, the provider and coordinator MUST run a final-close validator over the accumulated tool-call state.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:576:Only final-close success permits money-path settlement commit. Absence of any one required final-close condition is final-close failure. Mid-stream cap-cross, malformed final JSON, non-object final arguments, depth overflow, per-call cap overflow, aggregate cap overflow, partial-open end state, missing `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, missing normal completion marker, provider disconnect, timeout, relay error, authentication failure, truncation, or missing terminal marker after incremental-open is `FaultBreakerQualifying` and MUST settle zero provider-positive credits through the existing `phase4-coordinator/internal/buyer/billing_recorder.go:176` and `phase4-coordinator/internal/billing/formula.go:112` paths. These paths are unchanged by v0.2. Final-close failure MUST also produce no receipt for the turn and no sticky-route success write.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:584:If final-close fails after any tool-call delta has been emitted, the stream MUST terminate with an OpenAI-style `error` object on a terminating SSE event if the buyer connection can still be written, followed by `data: [DONE]`. The terminal-error SSE event MUST NOT carry `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. The chunk that crosses a cap or violates final-close MUST NOT be forwarded. Buyer SDKs, including `openai-python` v2.44.0+ and openai-node, MUST surface the terminal error frame as an exception or failed stream, not as a successful assistant message with dispatchable `tool_calls[]`. v0.2 may include internal failure reasons in logs and the terminating error object, but it MUST NOT expose the v0.3 `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call` schema.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:586:The buyer-visible streaming commit therefore happens at incremental-open; the settlement commit happens only at final-close. This preserves Cline-visible progress without allowing malformed or oversized provider output to earn provider-positive credits.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:634:AC-17. For non-streaming receipt-bearing responses, SPEC-015 v0.3 §5.1–§5.3 canonical output object includes canonicalized `tool_calls[]` when tool calls are emitted. (Streaming receipts are out of scope per SPEC-015 v0.3.)
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:642:AC-21. **Commit-worthy delta minimal-shape validation + DoS bounds (Security H-1 + Critic M-1).** The coordinator commit-signal code path (§8.4) MUST validate that any `delta.tool_calls[]` event chosen as commit-worthy has integer `index`, non-empty `id` string, `type == "function"`, non-empty `function.name`, and `function.arguments` as a JSON string whose decoded value is a JSON object with nesting depth ≤ 32 and byte length ≤ 256 KiB. Malformed or oversized pre-commit deltas — including `[{}]` (empty tool-call object), `{"function":{"arguments":"[]"}}` (arguments decodes to non-object), and `{"function":{"arguments":"<256-KiB-of-nested-objects>"}}` (exceeds depth or byte cap) — MUST NOT commit the response or settle provider-positive usage. Verified by a new coordinator test on the commit-signal path that rejects all three forms and accepts the minimal valid shape.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:652:AC-25a. **#1 Multi-turn end-to-end Cline release gate, CI-amenable fixture.** A headless Cline fixture using VS Code extension ID `saoudrizwan.claude-dev` / Cline v4.0.0 (or the exact version pinned in `tools/version-pins/cline-spec-018-v0_2_2.txt` if the marketplace patch version advances before IMPL lock), a pinned public test repo commit, and a pinned prompt runs through gateway → coordinator → v0.2 phase3 provider without a macprovider-specific Cline adapter. The fixture workspace MUST include `specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md` as a possible `read_file` target so the session can read content containing native tool-call markup without triggering any v0.2 prompt-echo self-DoS. The fixture MUST emit a machine-readable JSON session transcript with: Cline version, repo URL and commit, prompt SHA-256, ordered turns, raw OpenAI request/response or SSE transcript hashes, tool call IDs, tool categories, argument byte lengths, timing fields, provider/coordinator request IDs, streaming mode header, `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed` value per provider response, and pass/fail summary. Automated assertions require ≥ 20 provider turns after the initial user request, ≥ 30 total tool calls/results, tool categories covering directory listing/search, file read, file edit (full-write or patch), and shell command, ≥ 3 file edits across ≥ 2 files, ≥ 2 shell command runs with at least one failing command followed by a successful recovery turn, ≥ 1 assistant-history `tool_calls[]` echo plus matching `role:"tool"` result after turn 1, Cline session success whether `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed` is a known lowercase hex hash or `null`, no Cline branching on the value, and no `unsupported_tool_messages`, provider-side 5xx, malformed pre-commit tool delta, final-close failure, or missing `X-MacProvider-Streaming-Mode`. Fail condition: any criterion missing, transcript schema invalid, Cline behavior differs based on known-vs-unknown `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed`, SPEC-018 self-reading breaks a legitimate follow-up tool call, or a macprovider-specific Cline adapter is required.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:664:AC-29. **#1 Multi-turn receipt prompt-hash regression.** Non-streaming receipt regression tests prove that changing a replayed `tool_call_id` or assistant-history `tool_calls[]` changes `prompt_hash`. Fixture: two otherwise identical multi-turn requests differ only in one `tool_call_id`, then only in one assistant-history `function.arguments`; both changes produce distinct prompt hashes. Fail condition: either change leaves `prompt_hash` unchanged.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:674:AC-34. **#6 Buyer-fabricated ID acceptance.** A request with a buyer-fabricated assistant `tool_calls[].id` and matching `role:"tool".tool_call_id`, both matching `^call_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,64}$` and internally consistent, is accepted. The test asserts request acceptance only. Fail condition: rejection because the ID lacks provider provenance, or any retroactive settlement/receipt state is created for the fabricated prior event.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:690:AC-42. **#4 §8.4 split enforced.** Tests prove incremental-open runs before any `tool_calls[]` chunk is emitted and final-close gates provider-positive settlement. A malformed first delta fails before buyer-visible commit; a stream that passes incremental-open but fails final-close terminates with SSE error + `[DONE]` and zero provider-positive settlement. Fail condition: settlement commits at incremental-open or final-close is skipped.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:698:AC-46. **#2 Minimal model-hash binding observation.** Every provider response in v0.2 includes additive, non-canonicalized `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed`. Buyer-visible behavior is field-present plus JSON type-correct only: the value is `null | "^[a-f0-9]{64}$"`. This field is observation-only in v0.2 and MUST NOT drive v0.2 parser selection or settlement. It gives buyers and v0.3 registry work passive evidence to log the served `model_hash` against the modelID-declared family. Provider self-test: when the provider's own `model_hash` subsystem reports a known hash, the field MUST be that lowercase hex value; when unknown, the field MUST be `null`. AC-46 fixtures cover (a) buyer-side type assertion that every v0.2 response has the field present with type null or lowercase SHA-256 hex, and (b) provider-side log/release-gate assertion that known/unknown branches match the provider's local hash subsystem state. Fail condition: buyer-visible missing field, non-null non-hex value, inclusion in SPEC-015 canonical output binding, v0.2 enforcement based on a registry that §10c has explicitly deferred, or provider self-test mismatch against local `model_hash` state.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:700:AC-47. **#4 Final-close terminal completeness on provider EOF/disconnect.** For both `forwardWSStreaming` and `forwardStreaming`, after incremental-open has emitted or forwarded any `tool_calls[]` chunk, provider EOF/disconnect/timeout/relay error/authentication failure/truncation/missing terminal marker before all §8.4.2 terminal conditions are satisfied results in zero provider-positive credits, `FaultBreakerQualifying` recorded, no receipt, no sticky-route success write, and a terminal SSE error if the buyer connection can still be written. Fail condition: clean EOF alone is treated as final-close success, credits settle positive, receipt is emitted, sticky success is written, or either coordinator path lacks coverage.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:726:AC-60. **#743 Harmony completion-token accounting.** Harmony `usage.completion_tokens` counts only token IDs from `final` channel body spans that become buyer-visible assistant content, including the rule-5 visible-final truncation prefix when that narrow exception applies. Tool-call JSON body tokens, `analysis` body tokens, non-tool `commentary` body tokens, structural markers, headers, constrain labels, and call/end/return markers are excluded. A tool-call-only Harmony response has `completion_tokens = 0`. Fail condition: any hidden/tool-call/structural token contributes to `completion_tokens`, or emitted visible final-channel tokens are omitted from the count.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:835:    "settlement_ran": false
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:840:`param` MAY be omitted when no single request JSON path owns the failure. `retryable`, `inference_ran`, and `settlement_ran` are booleans. `request_id` MUST be the gateway/coordinator request identifier visible in logs.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:842:The codes in this table are buyer-visible HTTP/SSE error envelope codes. Internal plain-content fallback reasons are NOT buyer-visible error codes in v0.2 — they manifest as the absence of synthesized `tool_calls[]` plus normal plain assistant content. v0.2.3 deletes the v0.2.1 minimal prompt-echo guard and therefore has no `prompt_echo_blocked` buyer-visible or internal guard-trigger code path. v0.3 will expose malformed-tool-call diagnostics as a structured `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call.reason` enum.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:869:Every v0.2 provider response MUST include additive `usage.macprovider_model_hash_observed`. Buyer-visible validation is limited to field presence and JSON type `null | "^[a-f0-9]{64}$"`. Provider self-test MUST assert that the value is lowercase SHA-256 hex when the provider's local `model_hash` subsystem reports a known served model hash and `null` when that subsystem reports unknown. The field is non-canonicalized, observation-only, and MUST NOT affect v0.2 parser/profile selection, settlement, or SPEC-015 output binding. Its purpose is forward compatibility for the v0.3 registry: buyers can passively log the served `model_hash` against the modelID-declared family before registry enforcement exists. Cline and other OpenAI clients need not act on this field in v0.2; macprovider release evidence and logs capture it for diagnostics and v0.3 registry preparation.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:951:§8.4 defines the commit split. Incremental-open runs before any `tool_calls[]` chunk is emitted and permits buyer-visible streaming commit. Final-close runs at end-of-stream and gates money-path settlement commit. If final-close fails after emission, the stream terminates with an OpenAI-style `error` object on a terminating SSE event followed by `data: [DONE]` if the buyer connection can still be written; the error event MUST NOT carry `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`. Provider-output malformed deltas, mid-stream cap-cross, missing `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, missing transport terminal marker, provider disconnect/timeout/relay/auth failure/truncation after incremental-open, or any other final-close failure are `FaultBreakerQualifying` and settle zero provider-positive credits through existing `billing_recorder.go:176` and `formula.go:112` paths.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:1040:These four failures are request-validation failures. They are NOT fault-breaker-qualifying, MUST NOT run inference, MUST NOT commit provider credits, and MUST NOT produce a receipt.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:1046:Buyer-supplied assistant-history `tool_calls[]` and `role:"tool"` results are PROMPT DATA, NOT PROVIDER PROVENANCE. They MUST NOT create provider provenance, settlement entries, receipt output objects, or "provider emitted" audit claims for prior turns. Receipts for the current turn MAY bind the prompt hash that includes fabricated history, but MUST NOT attest that prior history was true or provider-minted.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:1076:- Deliverable #5 structured malformed-tool-call signal: buyer-visible `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call` schema, designed in `specs/v0_3-design/05-malformed-signal.md`.
specs/SPEC-018-agentic-tool-calling.md:1078:The internal failure reasons used by v0.2 in §8.4 split validation, §10d.4 streaming termination, and §10d.7 caps are intentionally named so they can map cleanly to the v0.3 structured `usage.macprovider_malformed_tool_call.reason` enum. v0.2 does not expose that structured usage signal; internal logs and terminating SSE error objects are the only v0.2 surfaces for those reasons.

specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:46:MacProvider today has a **strong integrity chain over the wrong root**. The catalog signing pipeline, the append-only release ledger, the model-hash consistency checks, the route snapshots, and the settlement receipts are all real and mostly well built — but every performance claim and almost every identity claim they protect originates as **provider self-report**. Signing, verifying, and receipting a self-reported number does not make it true; it makes it *tamper-evidently* self-reported.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:54:**Why the #744 provenance/signing work is not enough by itself** (required finding): PR #772 was the right *labeling* move, but it changes what we *say* about the numbers, not where they *come from*. Three specifics: (a) the provenance values in production are a **hardcoded client-side backfill table**, not signed catalog bytes — the signature covers zero provenance bytes, and the coordinator accepts nil and substitutes nothing; (b) provenance "does not by itself admit or reject cached benchmarks" (SPEC-023 §3.1) — metadata about an advisory field; (c) the enforcement pipeline (`ResolveMaxAdmission`, hash checks, settlement) never reads provenance at all. Signing harder or labeling better cannot fix a system whose admission evidence is fabricatable by construction (§4.2, §4.3).

specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:141:**Limit 1 — substitution.** Decode rate is `providerFirstByte → providerDone` over provider-emitted chunks (`phase_timing.go:213`); token counts come from the provider's own stream (`settlement_output.go:46-52`). A provider serving `qwen3-8b` while advertising `qwen3-32b`'s `model_id` and hash string **scores strictly better** on every latency metric than one honestly serving the larger model. The hash predicate does not stop it: `ws/server.go:906-910` is a case-insensitive string compare of a **provider-reported** hash.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:325:- **Pricing is UNRESOLVED and is the item's largest risk.** r2 said "discounted or unbilled." That is wrong as stated: provider payout derives from `provider_credits`, and `payout.go:118-128` **voids a payout row when `payableProvider < minPayoutCredits`** — so unbilled probation makes the provider serve for free and can void the payout outright, on a network whose scarce resource is providers. No discount mechanism exists (the only `discount` in billing is the cached-prompt-token one; the only unbilled path is the SPEC-022 `model_hash: null` *error* path). The candidate direction is **bill the buyer at full rate, escrow the provider's share, release on promotion and forfeit on demotion** — but that is new money-path work spanning `internal/billing/`, `phase5-gateway/` (`usage_events`, `ReservationSettlement`), and a SPEC-022/SPEC-005/SPEC-006 amendment. **Until that design exists, Brief B4 cannot be scoped.** Also invariant: probation pricing must never be buyer-selectable or buyer-visible pre-request, or a discount would attract buyers *to* unproven providers and distort the very data used to promote them.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:340:**Settlement non-retroactivity.** Ceiling and probation state are **non-retroactive for settlement**: requests served before an enforcement change are not retroactively repriced or clawed back, and in-flight requests at demotion complete and settle normally. This must be stated in the SPEC amendment so two implementers do not build opposite behaviors.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:415:This document went through four review rounds (r1→r4; two adversarial + two product-design Claude lanes, then codex security + architect). Each round the audit tally fell, but never to zero: every rewrite of the *single* roadmap spawned fresh CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM findings. The findings were not wording — they were structural, and they clustered on one signature: **the plan bundled a handful of small, independently-valuable, independently-verifiable fixes together with a large speculative trust subsystem (observed-performance routing + probationary admission) that rests on buyer-traffic volume nobody has measured.** Bundling them meant every audit found interaction defects — a probation state that the pool data model cannot express, a settlement path with no billing owner, a routing swap that misses a second self-report code path, an event taxonomy with no schema — and no amount of re-ranking a coupled list removes coupling.
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:445:- **Change**: correct §4.10's list; add a "what the catalog signature does not prove" section to SPEC-023 (mirroring the SPEC-015 receipts negative-list); amend SPEC-013 NFR-4 to enumerate the egress it omits (hardware-evidence POST, `/v1/rate-card`, signed static-feed fetches — the HF pre-warm carve-out is already at `SPEC-013:1280-1281`).
specs/trust-roadmap/RESEARCH-TRUST-MINIMIZED-BENCHMARK-CATALOG-ROADMAP.md:529:- **B4 — Probationary admission** (was R5). The largest brief and the one that must **not** be bundled with anything. Its SPEC must resolve, before any code: (1) a **new per-(provider, model) probation state** — `pool.Tier` is a per-provider scalar *and already the canary sanction state* (`pool/provider.go:1352`, `TierProvisional`→ban), and there is a *second* unrelated `rewards.TierProvisional`; neither can be reused; (2) a **pricing + settlement design** — probation traffic is proposed discounted/unbilled, but unbilled traffic yields zero `provider_credits` and can void payout under `minPayoutCredits` (`payout.go`), and no discount mechanism exists; this spans `internal/billing/`, `phase5-gateway/` (`usage_events`, `ReservationSettlement`), and a SPEC-022/005/006 amendment; (3) an **absolute** numeric exposure budget (§11 Q1) — relative caps give zero dilution at `pool_size: 1`; (4) anti-self-dealing that actually binds — the "≥2 payer accounts" rule is a two-account speed bump while registration is open (see B6), and the cited canarycorr prior art is provider-side, not payer-side; (5) grandfathering — existing providers are not retroactively placed in probation. The §6 flow is the *design sketch* feeding this brief; its Steps 0b/3/4 are proposals, and their appearance in §11 as open questions is correct, not a contradiction.

specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:43:SPEC-045 does not create a new public gateway, coordinator endpoint, provider serving path, settlement formula, rate-card source of truth, wallet session authority, provider payout rule, or model catalog authority.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:47:SPEC-045 does not authorize public-network listeners, daemon installation, background login items, shared multi-user service mode, credential issuance or rotation, provider-selection hints, raw receipt storage, or buyer-side token accounting as settlement evidence.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:63:SPEC-005 remains authoritative for billing formulas, rate math, settlement, token accounting, and provider payout. SPEC-045 may use trusted catalog/rate metadata only to make conservative local exposure-admission decisions and must not treat local estimates as settlement evidence.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:67:SPEC-015 remains authoritative for receipt privacy and retention. SPEC-045 may surface redacted request ids and local exposure ledger entries, but it must not persist raw prompts, raw completions, bearer tokens, full upstream errors, or raw receipt bodies.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:88:- Local budget admission is a conservative exposure control only; upstream MacProvider billing, settlement, gateway authentication, and quota authority remain with SPEC-005 and SPEC-006.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:101:- Logs, ledgers, status output, diagnostics, and cross-client error surfaces never persist or expose raw prompts, completions, bearer tokens, credential paths, raw receipts, full upstream bodies, local/private hostnames, usernames, or stable hardware identifiers. R006 separately allows the user-private active endpoint descriptor to contain the local token or same-security reference, and startup/status may show the bound loopback URL plus configured upstream origin. R007 separately allows the initiating local client to receive its own syntactically valid upstream error body.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:123:R002 implementations MUST enforce bounded aggregate post-authentication resource limits before request-body buffering or upstream dispatch. The limits MUST cover at least authenticated active request count, total buffered request-body bytes, total non-streaming response spool bytes, open streaming responses, worker tasks, and process file descriptors or sockets consumed by local endpoint mode. A request that would exceed an aggregate limit MUST fail locally as `local_endpoint_busy` without upstream forwarding and without reading more request-body bytes than needed to make the admission decision. Aggregate limits MUST be independent from the per-request size cap: an individual body over the selected per-request cap fails as `local_request_too_large`, while a conforming individual request rejected only because current aggregate usage is saturated fails as `local_endpoint_busy`.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:133:**SPEC-045-R004 - Conservative model and exposure admission.** The command MUST support an explicit local model allowlist and a cumulative local estimated-exposure limit expressed in USD-equivalent units through `--budget-usd <amount>`. `--budget-usd` is a local admission cap and is not a buyer billing balance, settlement ledger, payment authorization, refund rule, or source of truth for gateway charges. `--budget-usd 0`, negative values, non-finite values, and unparsable values MUST fail startup with a nonzero exit and redacted stderr error code `local_budget_flag_rejected`; they MUST NOT be silently treated as an exhausted budget or as `--no-budget`. Before forwarding a chargeable request, the command MUST require either a positive `--budget-usd <amount>` or an explicit `--no-budget` risk acknowledgement for the process, MUST check that the requested model is allowed, that the model appears in trusted upstream/catalog metadata, and that the request can be admitted without exceeding the remaining local exposure cap under a conservative exposure estimate. Admission-relevant fields, including `model`, `messages`, `max_tokens`, output-bound fields, `stream`, tool-calling fields, and structured-output fields, MUST be read only from the duplicate-key-free parse required by R002; an explicit JSON `null` output bound MUST be treated as absent and estimated from the model's trusted maximum output limit. Trusted pricing metadata for v0.1 means either a SPEC-006 public `GET /v1/rate-card` body paired with `GET /v1/rate-card.sig` that verifies as Ed25519 against the SPEC-023 repo-trusted static catalog keyring and satisfies SPEC-023 detached-sidecar, policy-version, and `generated_at` freshness rules, or a gateway quote/estimate result only if that quote/estimate surface is defined by SPEC-006 or a later dependency. Missing or malformed sidecars, unknown or retired key ids, non-Ed25519 algorithms, invalid signatures, policy mismatch, projection-hash mismatch, future-dated bytes beyond the SPEC-023 tolerance, rate-card bytes older than the SPEC-023 maximum age, or a fetched rate card older than the baked trusted snapshot MUST fail closed as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` applies. A trusted rate card MUST use the catalog release shape validated by `scripts/catalog-release.py`: top-level `version`, `policy_version`, `generated_at`, `usd_per_million_credits`, and non-empty `rows` containing a `default` row, with each row carrying `prompt_rate_per_mtok`, `prompt_cache_hit_rate_per_mtok`, `completion_rate_per_mtok`, `provider_share_bps`, and `global_multiplier_ppm`; its `version` MUST equal the rate-card projection hash, and model-key lookup MUST follow SPEC-005 §5.5 exact, normalized, then default resolution. A gateway `/v1/models` result is trusted only for model visibility and model id presence, not for price or output-limit authority. If the trusted rate card or trusted quote surface cannot supply price fields for the requested model or default row, or if a request lacks an explicit output bound and no trusted maximum output bound is available, budgeted admission MUST fail as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` applies. Unsigned local files, client request fields, or ad hoc environment values are not trusted metadata. Trusted metadata MUST be fetched at startup or before first admission and MAY be refreshed only at bounded implementation-defined intervals; it MUST NOT run as an unbounded background refresh loop. Before every chargeable admission, cached trusted pricing metadata MUST be revalidated against the local clock and SPEC-023 freshness rules. If the cached metadata has crossed the SPEC-023 stale-warning boundary, status MUST surface `stale_pricing` in the pricing warning-code list required by R006 while admission MAY continue until the reject boundary. If it has crossed the SPEC-023 maximum-age or future-skew reject boundary, the pricing trust state MUST be atomically marked `unavailable`, new chargeable admission MUST fail as `local_pricing_unavailable` unless `--allow-unpriced` can produce a conforming conservative reservation under R004, and the implementation MUST NOT continue admitting from expired cached pricing. The admission check and reservation write MUST be atomic within the process so no two concurrent requests can both pass admission before either one reduces the remaining budget. The estimate MUST use trusted catalog/rate metadata and request bounds such as `max_tokens` when available; it MUST NOT trust client-supplied prices, client-supplied token counts, provider hints, or response metadata as the source of cost authority. The conservative admission estimate MUST be the gross buyer-side USD-equivalent exposure, never provider payout or provider-share exposure. Arithmetic MUST use fixed-point integer or exact rational math with overflow detection; overflow, precision loss, missing operands, non-finite values, or any under-reserving ambiguity MUST fail closed as `local_pricing_unavailable`. For v0.1, prompt cost MUST be estimated as `estimated_prompt_tokens * prompt_rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000` using the full `prompt_rate_per_mtok`; cached-token discounts from `prompt_cache_hit_rate_per_mtok` MUST NOT be applied unless a trusted gateway quote/estimate surface defined by SPEC-006 or a later dependency distinguishes trusted cache-hit token counts. Completion cost MUST be `bounded_completion_tokens * completion_rate_per_mtok / 1_000_000`. The sum MUST then apply `global_multiplier_ppm` multiplicatively as in SPEC-005 gross-credit math, converted through trusted `usd_per_million_credits` when credits-to-USD conversion is needed, and rounded upward to the smallest representable local ledger unit before reservation. `provider_share_bps` MUST NOT reduce the buyer exposure estimate. Prompt exposure MUST be estimated from the submitted request body using a trusted gateway estimate, a tokenizer bound to the requested model's trusted catalog identity, or a byte-to-token upper bound no less conservative than one UTF-8 byte equals one token. Completion exposure MUST use the request's explicit output bound when present; when no bound is present, it MUST use the model's trusted maximum output limit, and if that limit is unavailable budgeted mode MUST reject the request as `local_pricing_unavailable`. When trusted pricing is unavailable and a positive run budget is configured, the request MUST fail closed unless the operator supplied an explicit unpriced-request override for that run using `--allow-unpriced`. Under `--allow-unpriced` with a positive run budget, each unpriced chargeable request MUST reserve the entire remaining local budget before forwarding, ledger `admission estimate` MUST equal the pre-request remaining budget, status remaining budget MUST become zero until settlement/recovery changes it, concurrent unpriced chargeable admissions MUST fail as `local_budget_exceeded` while that reservation is active, and if trusted upstream usage/cost evidence remains unavailable at terminal settlement the reservation MUST settle to that full admission estimate. Any `--no-budget` or unpriced-request override MUST be shown at startup, included in local status, recorded in the ledger when a ledger is active, and surfaced as a warning before or with each affected chargeable request using response header `X-MacProvider-Warning` with value `no_budget` or `unpriced_override`; this warning header MUST NOT alter the OpenAI JSON or SSE body. If an upstream response already contains `X-MacProvider-Warning`, the local warning value MUST be appended as a distinct comma-separated token without deleting upstream warning values.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:139:R004 canonical local budget precision is micro-USD. All run budget, reservation, settlement, held, released, remaining, and per-request cap arithmetic MUST use signed integer counts of micro-USD (`1e-6` USD) as the canonical local ledger unit. Ledger rows MUST record amount fields as string-encoded integer micro-USD values, including `admission_estimate_micro_usd`, `settled_exposure_micro_usd`, and any budget delta fields, and MUST NOT use JSON floating-point numbers for monetary ledger state.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:141:**SPEC-045-R005 - Restart-safe budget ledger.** When a cumulative run budget is configured, the command MUST persist a local exposure ledger under the default user-private state path `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume/ledgers/default.jsonl` on macOS unless the operator supplies an explicit ledger path, and it MUST hold an OS-enforced exclusive advisory file lock on a lock file named `<ledger-filename>.lock` adjacent to the ledger. The lock MUST use OS lock state, not lockfile presence; a stale lock file from a crashed process MUST NOT prevent a new process from acquiring the lock after the OS releases the prior lock on process termination. Ledger path class values MUST be the closed enum `default_user_state`, `explicit_absolute`, or `explicit_relative`; explicit relative ledger paths MUST resolve relative to the current working directory captured at process startup. The implementation MUST refuse any mode that creates a ledger, including budgeted mode and `--no-budget --ledger <path>`, when the state path is not user-private, is symlink-ambiguous, is not on a local filesystem with verified exclusive-lock semantics, or cannot be locked by exactly one active process. Implementations MUST verify local filesystem lock support using OS metadata such as `statfs`/`fstatfs` or a stronger platform-specific check, and MUST fail closed when the filesystem type or mount properties cannot be verified as local with real exclusive-lock semantics. A state path is symlink-ambiguous when the ledger path, lock path, or any parent directory resolves through a symlink that is not owned by the current OS user, or when the resolved target changes between validation and open/lock. Passing `--ledger <path>` without either `--budget-usd <amount>` or `--no-budget` MUST fail startup with `local_budget_flag_rejected` rather than creating an idle ledger whose admission mode is ambiguous. When `--no-budget` is combined with an explicit `--ledger <path>`, the ledger MUST be created, locked, and written with per-request no-budget records; the ledger path class is `explicit_absolute` or `explicit_relative` as appropriate. When `--no-budget` is used without an explicit `--ledger`, no ledger is created and per-request no-budget state is in-memory only. The ledger MUST record schema version `local_consumer_endpoint.ledger.v1`, immutable process launch id (`run_id`), a unique local `reservation_id` generated from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG input for every reservation, the same `run_id` and `reservation_id` copied onto every later state transition and audit row for that reservation, redacted request ids, model id, admission estimate or JSON null when `--no-budget` skips admission estimation, unpriced-override flag, no-budget flag when applicable, terminal local outcome, settled exposure amount when known, upstream request id when available, reservation state (`reserved`, `settled`, `held`, `released`, or `estimate_exceeded`), and created/updated timestamps; it MUST NOT record raw prompts, raw completions, bearer tokens, local bearer tokens, raw receipts, full upstream error bodies, hostnames, OS usernames, hardware serials, MAC addresses, or stable hardware UUIDs. A budgeted admission reservation MUST NOT be considered committed and MUST NOT be forwarded upstream until the ledger reservation append is durable; durable means the append bytes and required file metadata have been flushed with `fsync()` or a platform-equivalent durability primitive on the ledger file descriptor, and any newly created parent directory entry has been flushed with a platform-equivalent directory sync where supported. Every ledger state-transition append, including settlement, `estimate_exceeded`, held, released, and recovery audit entries, MUST satisfy the same durability rule before any local HTTP response, status output, recovery-command output, remaining-budget value, or restart-recovery decision relies on that transition. If a durable append fails, including fsync failure, the implementation MUST roll back any affected in-process reservation state when possible, mark ledger health unhealthy, return `local_budget_ledger_unavailable` for runtime chargeable paths, fail recovery commands nonzero without claiming success, and stop accepting chargeable requests until ledger health is restored. After a terminal upstream response, the ledger MUST settle a reservation to trusted upstream usage/cost evidence when such evidence is available, even when that evidence exceeds the admission estimate; if trusted usage/cost evidence is unavailable, it MUST settle to the admission estimate rather than inventing a lower cost. If trusted upstream usage/cost evidence exceeds the admission estimate, the ledger MUST record state `estimate_exceeded`, remaining budget MUST be allowed to reach zero or a negative value, status MUST surface the pricing-invariant breach, and the process MUST stop accepting new chargeable admission requests until restarted with corrected trusted pricing metadata or an explicit operator recovery path defined by a later spec; in-flight requests that already passed admission before `estimate_exceeded` was set MUST be allowed to complete. SPEC-005 billing and settlement remain authoritative. If the local client disconnects during streaming before trusted terminal usage/cost evidence is available, the implementation MUST cancel or close the upstream request when possible, wait no longer than one second for synchronous cancellation acknowledgement, and settle the reservation to the admission estimate unless the upstream returns trusted partial usage/cost evidence bound to the request. In-flight reservations MUST be treated conservatively on process restart: they become `held` and reduce remaining budget until a recovery command updates them. On graceful shutdown, including SIGTERM, the process MUST stop accepting new requests, drain in-flight requests for a bounded period no longer than five seconds, settle terminal requests, cancel or close remaining upstream requests, mark remaining in-flight reservations `held`, remove the active endpoint descriptor when possible, and then exit. Operators should expect long-running streaming requests that exceed the five-second drain bound to become held reservations requiring recovery-command handling; that operational cost is intentional in v0.1 because bounded shutdown takes precedence over waiting indefinitely. R005 conformance REQUIRES local recovery commands named `malibu-cli consume budget status` and `malibu-cli consume budget release-held`; `status` MUST show redacted held reservations, age, estimate, and ledger path class, while `release-held` MUST require a ledger selector `--ledger <path>` or `--ledger default`, a run selector `--run-id <process-launch-id>`, and `--confirm-release-held`, MUST fail rather than modify the ledger while another process holds the ledger lock, MUST only release held local reservations whose immutable `run_id` exactly matches that selected run, MUST append a redacted audit entry carrying the same `run_id` and each released `reservation_id`, MUST leave wrong-run and missing-reservation rows unchanged, and MUST NOT alter settled local exposure or upstream gateway records. `--ledger default` on recovery commands MUST resolve to the macOS default path computed at recovery-command invocation time from the invoking user's `$HOME`. Manual ledger deletion is not a conformant recovery path. If the ledger cannot be opened, locked, parsed, or written, budgeted mode MUST refuse to start or MUST stop accepting chargeable requests.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:143:R005 ledger rows MUST be self-describing: every ledger row, including reservation, transition, settlement, held, released, `estimate_exceeded`, and audit rows, MUST include `schema_version: "local_consumer_endpoint.ledger.v1"`. There is no separate header row. Recovery commands MUST validate `schema_version` before acting on a row and MUST skip rows with unknown or missing schema versions while reporting a redacted warning code.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:149:For non-streaming chat-completions settlement, trusted terminal usage/cost evidence means a complete upstream JSON response body that satisfies all R002/R007 response bounds, is not truncated or protocol-invalid, and contains a SPEC-006/OpenAI-compatible `usage` object or SPEC-006-defined cost metadata bound to that response. A partial, truncated, unparsable, protocol-invalid, or locally cap-rejected non-streaming response MUST NOT supply trusted settlement evidence.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:151:For SSE streaming settlement, trusted terminal usage/cost evidence means either usage data in the final event frame or usage data from an earlier event frame that is confirmed by a subsequent `data: [DONE]` on the same upstream response. Usage data before `data: [DONE]` MAY be cached but MUST NOT finalize settlement by itself. If `data: [DONE]` arrives without trusted usage evidence, or the stream terminates before `data: [DONE]`, settlement MUST follow the conservative R005 admission-estimate rule.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:153:**SPEC-045-R006 - Local status and diagnostics.** The local server MUST expose local status at `GET /v1/status` on the same loopback listener and MUST support `malibu-cli consume status` for CLI status output. On startup, the process MUST generate a process launch id as a lowercase RFC4122 UUID v4 from at least 128 bits of CSPRNG input, yielding 122 bits of effective UUID v4 randomness, MUST keep it stable only for that process lifetime, and MUST write a user-private instance descriptor to `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume/active-endpoint.json` on macOS containing only the bound loopback URL, process id, process launch id, started-at timestamp, ledger path class, and the per-run local bearer token or a same-security token reference so `consume status` can locate and authenticate to the active endpoint. Concurrent local endpoint instances are unsupported in v0.1: before acquiring or creating the descriptor or lock, the implementation MUST verify that `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume` and each relevant parent directory selected for active endpoint state are current-user-owned, not writable by other users, not symlink-ambiguous under the R005 symlink rule, and stable between validation, open, write, rename, and lock acquisition. Startup MUST acquire an OS-enforced exclusive advisory lock on `$HOME/Library/Application Support/macprovider/consume/active-endpoint.lock` before reading, validating, or writing the descriptor, MUST hold that lock until process exit, and MUST fail with redacted stderr error code `local_active_endpoint_exists` when another live process holds the lock or when an existing active descriptor points to a live process with a matching launch id. The descriptor lock MUST use OS lock state, not lockfile presence, so a stale lock file from a crashed process does not block startup after the OS releases the lock. The instance descriptor MUST be written atomically by creating a temporary file in the same directory with user-only read/write permissions before any bytes are written, then renaming it to `active-endpoint.json`; stale descriptors MUST be ignored when the process id or launch id no longer matches, because process launch id protects against process-id reuse. `malibu-cli consume status` MUST return a nonzero exit and redacted message code `local_endpoint_not_running` when no descriptor exists or all discovered descriptors are stale. Status MUST report schema version `local_consumer_endpoint.status.v1`, process launch id, bound loopback URL, upstream gateway origin, credential-source class, credential state (`missing`, `loaded`, or `invalid_or_expired`), model allowlist, pricing trust state (`trusted`, `unpriced_override`, `unavailable`, or `estimate_exceeded`), pricing warning codes as a closed bounded list including `stale_pricing` when the R004 stale-warning boundary is crossed, local-auth state (`required` or `rejected` only, never token material), unpriced-override state, no-budget acknowledgement state, budget configured/used/held/remaining, ledger path class, active request count, last successful upstream contact wall-clock time, and a redacted bounded error ring containing at least the last five and at most the last 100 local/upstream error code classes. Every `GET /v1/status` response MUST include `Cache-Control: no-store`. An error code class is only the local error `error.code` string or the upstream SPEC-006 `error.type`/`error.code` string, plus a redacted canonical request id when available; each field MUST have a fixed maximum length, the ring MUST enforce both entry-count and total-byte limits, and it MUST NOT include error messages or body fragments. When no budget is configured because the operator selected `--no-budget`, budget configured/used/held/remaining MUST be represented as JSON null values rather than zero, ledger path class MUST be JSON null only when no explicit ledger path was selected, and status MUST display an explicit no-budget warning. If `--no-budget` is combined with an explicit ledger path, or a recovery/status command selected an explicit ledger path, ledger path class MUST be `explicit_absolute` or `explicit_relative` as appropriate. Status and diagnostics may freely include the configured upstream gateway origin because it is operator-supplied endpoint configuration and not a secret; they MUST omit bearer tokens, local bearer tokens, raw prompts, raw completions, full credential paths, raw receipts, full upstream response bodies, local/private hostnames, OS usernames, hardware serials, MAC addresses, stable hardware UUIDs, and network interface names. Status MUST distinguish local-auth rejection, local-budget rejection, local-model rejection, missing credential, upstream authentication failure, upstream quota/rate-limit failure, upstream transport failure, unsupported local endpoint, and estimate-exceeded pricing invariant failure.
specs/SPEC-045-local-consumer-endpoint-mode.md:157:**SPEC-045-R007 - Gateway error preservation and local error codes.** Upstream SPEC-006 errors and any syntactically valid upstream HTTP response, regardless of status code, MUST be proxied to the same local client under the preservation rule rather than being converted into local success or `local_upstream_unavailable`; `local_upstream_unavailable` applies only to transport failures and protocol-invalid responses. The local endpoint MAY return the upstream error body to the same local client that initiated the request, but logs, status, ledger rows, diagnostics, and other clients MUST receive only redacted error code/class/request-id material. Startup failures MUST return process exit codes and stderr error codes, not HTTP envelopes. Local-only HTTP failures MUST use an OpenAI-shaped error envelope with `error.type`, `error.message`, nullable `error.param`, `error.code`, and an extension object `error.macprovider` containing boolean `forwarded_upstream`, except `HEAD` responses MUST have an empty body regardless of error code. Local HTTP error codes MUST map as follows: `local_auth_required` to 401, `local_credential_missing` to 401, `local_invalid_request` to 400, `local_content_encoding_unsupported` to 415, `local_model_not_allowed` to 400, `local_pricing_unavailable` to 503, `local_budget_required` to 400, `local_request_too_large` to 413, `local_endpoint_busy` to 503, `local_budget_exceeded` to 402, `local_budget_ledger_unavailable` to 503, `local_estimate_exceeded` to 503, `local_endpoint_unsupported` to 404 or 405 as appropriate for the path/method, and `local_upstream_unavailable` to 502 when the upstream returns an unparseable or protocol-invalid response, closes before returning response headers, or returns response headers for a non-streaming response but the body is truncated by reset or EOF before any local response body bytes are sent, and to 503 when the upstream is unreachable or times out before returning response headers. Once a streaming `text/event-stream` response has sent local response headers or body bytes, the implementation MUST NOT attempt to change the HTTP status to 502; on upstream reset, EOF, or protocol-invalid truncation after that point it MUST emit a terminal SSE error event carrying redacted `local_upstream_unavailable` code material when the local connection is still writable, then close the stream and settle the ledger conservatively under R005. `local_bind_rejected`, `local_credential_flag_rejected`, `local_budget_flag_rejected`, `local_upstream_url_rejected`, and `local_active_endpoint_exists` are reserved only for startup failure and MUST NOT be returned by a running HTTP server. Local response headers forwarded from the upstream gateway MUST be allowlisted to OpenAI/SPEC-006 compatibility metadata: content type, upstream `Content-Encoding` when body bytes remain encoded, upstream `Cache-Control`, rate-limit and retry headers, request id, receipt header, streaming-mode header, and other explicitly named `X-MacProvider-*` response metadata defined by SPEC-006, SPEC-015, SPEC-018, or a later dependency; the local warning header `X-MacProvider-Warning` MAY be added by SPEC-045. `Content-Encoding` MUST accompany the upstream body bytes verbatim when forwarded. `Cache-Control` MUST be forwarded only when received from upstream, and the local proxy MUST NOT add a permissive cache policy locally. Local errors MUST identify whether the request was forwarded upstream through `error.macprovider.forwarded_upstream`; local-only errors set it to `false`, and locally generated upstream-transport errors set it to `true` only after request bytes were sent upstream. The same `local_upstream_unavailable` code may appear with either `forwarded_upstream` value depending on whether the transport failure occurred before or after request bytes were sent upstream. The implementation MUST NOT retry non-idempotent chat completions after bytes have been sent upstream unless the gateway supplies an idempotency contract and the request is bound to it; before bytes are sent, it MAY perform at most one bounded connection attempt per upstream request before returning `local_upstream_unavailable`.

specs/design/spec-040/BUILD_SPEC_040_WALLET_NATIVE_BUYER_SESSIONS_IMPL.md:7:Ship a default-off gateway wallet-session rail that lets an existing gateway account authorize a wallet-held bounded buyer session, then use a short-lived `mps_` session bearer plus session-key signatures for inference requests. Usage must settle through existing gateway quota reservations, `usage_events`, settlement journal, coordinator `request_log.external_request_id`, receipts, and billing surfaces. Existing API-key behavior must remain unchanged.

specs/design/spec-040/BUILD_SPEC_040_WALLET_NATIVE_BUYER_SESSIONS_IMPL.md:63:   Add wallet-session read methods to `router.ReadStore` and storage read interfaces. GET list/status/usage handlers must use `s.readStore()`; POST/DELETE/admission/settlement stay on the write store. All wallet-session routes, session-filtered `/v1/models`, and wallet-session errors containing account/session state must set `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Pragma: no-cache`, and a `Vary` header that includes at least `Authorization` and `X-Api-Key` while preserving existing values such as `Origin`. Browser-visible CORS preflight for mounted wallet-session-capable routes must allow `X-MacProvider-Session-Timestamp` and `X-MacProvider-Session-Signature`. Demo/operator credentials must not create/list/revoke wallet sessions in v0.1.

specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:67:SPEC-043 does not define Privacy Pools. specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:89:**SPEC-043-R002 - Creator root issuer registration.** A creator MUST register exactly one stable root issuer public key per pool identity before the first policy manifest is accepted. Root-registration nonce issuance, root registration, root retirement, and custody-disclosure mutation MUST be gated on enabled creator state, current approval version, and the requested launch environment. Root-compromise reporting MUST NOT be gated on creator-enabled state, Creator Agreement validity, or launch eligibility; it MUST use a separately authenticated emergency channel that remains usable while the creator is disabled, suspended, expired, or under investigation. The registration MUST bind creator account id, current approval version, root issuer key id, root issuer public key fingerprint, root signature algorithm, proof-of-possession signature, delegated SPEC-042 manifest authority root key id, delegated SPEC-042 manifest authority root public key, structured key custody disclosure hash, genesis nonce digest, intended pool display name hash, launch environment, and approval record id. The canonical field `root_issuer_public_key_fingerprint` MUST be `SHA256(domain || u16_be_len(algorithm_id) || algorithm_id || u32_be_len(canonical_public_key_bytes) || canonical_public_key_bytes)`, where `domain` is the exact ASCII string `macprovider/spec043/root-issuer-key/v1`; the SPEC-043 root algorithm registry contains exactly one MVP `algorithm_id`, `ecdsa-p256-sha256`, encoded as ASCII bytes and using DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo public-key bytes; any additional algorithm_id or non-SPKI public-key encoding requires a SPEC-043 amendment before acceptance; and `canonical_public_key_bytes` is the single DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo encoding for MVP; key ids, JSON encoding, whitespace, and registration-envelope fields MUST NOT affect the fingerprint. The coordinator MUST reject root issuer public-key fingerprint reuse across every non-test SPEC-043 registration unless the earlier registration is the same pool identity and the operation is an idempotent replay of the already accepted bundle. The coordinator MUST maintain a durable root-fingerprint lineage index covering every registration, pool, signer set, routeable snapshot, and tombstone descended from that fingerprint, and lineage indexes plus tombstones MUST key on `root_issuer_public_key_fingerprint`. The proof-of-possession input MUST be a versioned, domain-separated canonical structure `RootKeyRegistrationV1` containing an exact published field list for every registration-bundle field except the proof-of-possession signature field, plus nonce, nonce expiry, purpose, creator account id, and environment; `RootKeyRegistrationV1` MUST be encoded as RFC 8785 canonical JSON with lexicographically sorted member names and no unknown fields; the exact signed field set is creator_account_id, current_approval_version, root_issuer_key_id, root_issuer_public_key_fingerprint, root_signature_algorithm, manifest_authority_root_key_id, manifest_authority_root_public_key, structured_key_custody_disclosure_hash, genesis_nonce_digest, intended_pool_display_name_hash, launch_environment, approval_record_id, nonce, nonce_expiry, purpose, and environment, excluding only the proof-of-possession signature field. The delegated SPEC-042 manifest authority root public key MUST be the Ed25519 root issuer key consumed by SPEC-042 authority-log and policy-history verification; the SPEC-043 P-256 root signature proves creator control of the externally registered root and binds that root to the SPEC-042 authority lineage without replacing SPEC-042's Ed25519 manifest primitives. The coordinator MUST atomically consume the one-time nonce, reject expired or purpose-mismatched nonces, verify the proof-of-possession signature over the domain-separated commitment using the submitted root issuer public key, reject the registration before persisting any bundle field if signature verification fails, and reject any registration whose authenticated creator session does not match the `creator_account_id` in the signed bundle. MacProvider MUST provide a documented root-key generation procedure or CLI that produces a registration bundle without exposing private-key material to MacProvider. The identity genesis nonce MUST contain at least 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy before hashing, so `pool_id` values are non-enumerable and cannot be guessed from creator/product names alone. `key_custody_disclosure` MUST include at least `{class, description}` where class is one of `software`, `hsm`, `mpc`, or `other`; production activation MUST require a MacProvider-approved custody class, and `software` custody is allowed only for isolated candidate or explicitly approved exception pools that are buyer-visible as such. Software-custody exceptions MUST be recorded in the creator approval record as `isolated_candidate_only` or `signed_exception_with_expiry`; a signed exception MUST include an expiry timestamp, the coordinator MUST schedule gate re-evaluation at that timestamp, and an expired exception MUST fail the R008 custody gate with reason `custody_exception_expired` until renewed or replaced by non-software custody. The root issuer private key MUST never be uploaded to MacProvider, and registration endpoints MUST reject payloads that parse as private-key material. Root issuer loss and compromise are separate cases: loss requires MacProvider-approved retirement, a MacProvider-signed continuity or non-continuity attestation, and new-pool registration with buyer-visible manual lineage signed by MacProvider but explicitly not signed by the lost root. Compromise notification MUST enter through an authenticated, rate-limited MacProvider compromise-notification intake surface; unauthenticated requests MUST be rejected before recording receipt. Every authenticated root-compromise assertion MUST trigger a provisional emergency freeze within 30 seconds of the intake surface recording an immutable receipt timestamp, and the freeze audit log entry MUST bind that timestamp; qualification and investigation MAY follow only after the freeze is active. During a root-compromise freeze, the coordinator MUST suspend creator-admin operations for every affected creator and pool, including nonce issuance, root registration, root retirement, custody mutation, policy submission, signer rotation, member admission, buyer-authorization mutation, lifecycle transition, and pool activation, rejecting them with reason `root_compromise_freeze` unless the operation is the independent MacProvider terminal-retirement path defined below. Manual break-glass is only a fallback and MUST also complete within 30 seconds of the operator receiving a paged alert. Compromise requires immutable retirement epoch/tombstone outside rollback-removable pool state, terminal retirement of the entire root-derived authority lineage, and rejection of every descendant operational signer with no exceptions from root-derived credentials; if the compromised fingerprint appears in the lineage index, freeze and terminal retirement MUST apply to every registration, pool, signer set, and snapshot descended from that fingerprint. Retirement and recovery operations during and after compromise freeze MUST use an independent MacProvider operator credential verified against the MacProvider operator credential registry, not any descendant signer set. The sole permitted retirement signer is a pre-registered MacProvider operator credential whose scope is restricted to publishing a terminal retirement attestation for the compromised root identity and co-signing the MacProvider-issued continuity or non-continuity attestation; this signer MUST NOT be co-resident with or derivable from compromised root material, MUST be pre-registered independently of the pool root key, and MUST expire when the terminal retirement attestation is issued. A root issuer MUST NOT be rotated in place.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:99:**SPEC-043-R007 - Buyer authorization.** A buyer may select a pool only if the buyer's credential is authorized for that `pool_id`. For live external creator pools, authorization MUST be per API key or a dedicated pool-only buyer account whose disclosure and isolation are recorded in the creator admin surface and signed journey evidence; broad account-level config is acceptable only for isolated candidate tests unless this spec is amended. The storage model MUST preserve enough structure to migrate from dedicated-account MVP to per-key scopes without widening access. If per-key scope migration is not implemented in the candidate environment, the signed journey MUST record that as a blocking V1 dependency and live external pools MUST remain on dedicated pool-only buyer accounts until the migration journey is rerun successfully. `pool_id` is a non-capability identifier, not a bearer secret; the pool distribution package MUST state how authorized buyers receive it and that access is credential-bound. Unauthorized, unknown, disabled, stale, or unavailable pool selections MUST return the generic SPEC-042 `pool_unavailable` response without revealing whether the pool exists. The gateway and coordinator MUST check credential scope before any existence-dependent lookup; the gateway scope check MUST evaluate authorization for the specific requested `pool_id`, not merely that the buyer credential is globally active, and forwarding to the coordinator for per-pool authorization is prohibited when that gateway scope check rejects. The coordinator MUST provide or signal buyer-authorization generation to the gateway on every creator-admin buyer-authorization mutation, and the gateway MUST refresh buyer authorization state for the affected `pool_id` within 30 seconds; gateway cache lifetime for buyer authorization state MUST NOT exceed 30 seconds. Rejections MUST use an identical serialized negative response, status, header names and values, padded content length, cache policy, retry metadata, and lookup path across unknown, unauthorized, disabled, stale, and wallet-session-rejected pools. Implementations MUST enforce a minimum response floor using an active timing mechanism for every rejection path. The floor MUST be at least the p99 latency of authorized pool-selection requests measured at the gateway in the candidate environment and no less than 50 ms from request receipt to response-commitment-decision-to-send; the signed journey MUST record the floor value, method, and baseline distribution. Before opening live external traffic on any pool, the gateway floor MUST be re-measured in the production configuration and updated to at least the observed production p99 authorized pool-selection latency; if production p99 exceeds the candidate-derived floor, a proportional floor adjustment MUST be applied and the timing journey step MUST be rerun in the production configuration before external traffic is accepted. Optimization of any path, floor change between candidate and production, or production latency distribution change that raises authorized p99 above the configured floor MUST include proportional floor adjustment, invalidate the timing test, and require the timing journey step to be rerun. The signed journey MUST run a repeated-sample distribution test over those rejection classes and fail if the response-commitment-decision-to-send p95 delta exceeds 15 ms, p99 delta exceeds 25 ms, or a two-sample statistical test specified by the journey harness distinguishes classes at p < 0.01. Wallet sessions MUST be rejected for pool selection until a SPEC-040 amendment signs the pool binding and a SPEC-043 amendment explicitly unlocks wallet pool selection.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:102:The reviewed creator distribution artifact MUST cover creator-owned app screens, buyer onboarding copy, launch URL or distribution package, and external product claims submitted for the launch; missing, stale, changed, or prohibited-claim artifacts MUST fail production activation and public-announcement approval until reviewed again. A candidate-only activation transition MAY be used solely inside the isolated candidate environment to generate the first signed journey result; it MUST require every technical gate except completed journey/promotion evidence, MUST be impossible to target production or publicly announced visibility, and MUST mark all traffic, receipts, and artifacts as candidate-only.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:105:Mismatches in candidate build ids, schema/migration hash, environment id/class, governance-file digest, `pool_id`, approval record id/version, Creator Agreement expiry/grace timestamps, reviewed creator distribution artifact digest, pricing schedule id/version, manifest version/digest, routeable snapshot digest, pool generation, feature-flag digest, buyer-authorization version, membership/delegation version, retention policy id/version, claim-control artifact digest, binary/trust predicate digest, settlement rate-card identity, production timing floor value or timing-baseline digest, or any route/auth/settlement/promise/emergency-behavior field MUST require a fresh signed candidate journey and MUST NOT be resolved by a fresh promotion authorization alone, even when the journey TTL has not expired; Agreement expiry/grace timestamps are runtime-affecting unless the canonical timestamp values are byte-identical to the candidate evidence.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:106:Promotion-only refresh MAY be accepted only for Creator Agreement id/version and gate-check id changes that are proven by a machine-readable diff with `runtime_effect=false` and no route, authorization, settlement, promise-surface, retention, claim-control, emergency, feature-flag, binary, predicate, membership, or Agreement expiry/grace timestamp effect; otherwise a fresh candidate journey is required.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:111:**SPEC-043-R009 - Promise surfaces, visibility, and claim control.** Before live traffic, the pool MUST expose creator-signed `pool_policy.json` and coordinator-attested `pool_status.json` as required by SPEC-042. Each pool MUST declare visibility mode `private`, `authorized`, or `publicly_announced`. For `private` and `authorized` pools, policy/status lookup MUST use the same non-enumerating unauthorized/unknown behavior and timing/cache controls as pool selection; public unauthenticated exposure requires explicit approved `publicly_announced` state. These surfaces MUST disclose creator provenance, MVP mode `single_operator`, `supply_mode`, co-tenancy or dedicated-supply status, `min_eligible_members`, current eligible member count, root issuer custody class, `split_execution_status`, confidentiality scope, retention-policy id, enforced predicates, observe-only predicates, and current readiness. The root issuer custody class MUST come immutably from the R002 registration record, MUST be one of `software`, `hsm`, `mpc`, or `other`, MUST NOT be mutated by pool updates, and MUST be visible to authorized buyers under the same controls as other policy fields; software-custody exception pools MUST include a human-readable note that the pool root issuer key is held in software storage. For pools where active `min_eligible_members` is 1, the promise surfaces MUST explicitly state that the pool has no high-availability guarantee and that a single eligible member outage will cause pool-required traffic to fail closed. The retention-policy id MUST resolve to a MacProvider-registered retention policy record with field categories, minimum/maximum retention periods, deletion SLA, and governing policy version; unknown retention policies MUST fail activation. The retention policy registered for a pool MUST declare a minimum retention period for R010 dispute audit trail categories that equals or exceeds the Creator Agreement dispute window; the coordinator MUST reject activation if request log, route snapshot, settlement record, provider receipt, or pool audit log retention minimums are shorter than that dispute window. `pool_status.json` MUST be regenerated within 30 seconds of membership, lifecycle, policy, creator suspension, predicate-state, signer-set, retention-policy, reviewed creator distribution artifact, binary/trust predicate, break-glass, on-call readiness expiry, Agreement expiry/grace, or any other R008 route-affecting mutation, and a pool whose status freshness exceeds 300 seconds MUST fail closed until refreshed. `pool_policy.json` and `pool_status.json` MUST use cache controls that preserve freshness enforcement, such as `Cache-Control: no-store` or `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, and any CDN path MUST not serve stale data beyond the fail-closed threshold. MacProvider MUST document the maximum expected coordinator restart duration and MUST provide creators at least the Creator Agreement's planned-maintenance notice before events whose duration may cause `pool_status.json` staleness to exceed 300 seconds. If planned maintenance will exceed 300 seconds, MacProvider MUST proactively transition affected pools to lifecycle `paused` with reason `scheduled_maintenance` before maintenance begins and restore lifecycle `active` within the recovery window declared in the Creator Agreement after maintenance completes. Promise surfaces MUST state that prompts/responses are visible to the coordinator and selected provider operator, and that `supply_mode: "shared"` means providers may also serve global traffic. Claim-control validation MUST run on every initial manifest, policy update, mutable operational field update, promise-surface update, and creator-submitted disclosure. For technical claim-control enforcement, `creator-submitted disclosure` is limited to structured content submitted through the creator admin surface, including buyer-visible disclosure text configured in pool records and policy documents. External marketing and sales materials are governed by the Creator Agreement prohibition referenced in R001, but production activation and public-announcement approval MUST additionally bind a reviewed distribution artifact digest under R008 so launch-time external claims cannot bypass pre-live review. Any claim of Privacy Pool, anonymous routing, coordinator-blind content, end-to-end encryption, confidential compute, zero-knowledge inference, ZK inference, dedicated supply without dedicated members, isolated compute without dedicated members, or regulated compliance such as HIPAA, GLBA, SOC 2, PCI-DSS, GDPR adequacy, or equivalent vertical-specific regulatory compliance MUST fail acceptance. A `pool_policy.json` that omits root issuer custody class or presents a value inconsistent with the registered custody disclosure MUST fail acceptance.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:113:**SPEC-043-R010 - Settlement and payout boundaries.** MVP settlement MUST carry immutable `pool_id` context sufficient for audit and reconciliation, but MUST NOT represent declared `revenue_split_bps` as executed payout. `split_execution_status` MUST be `declared_not_executed` unless SPEC-005 and SPEC-016 amendments implement creator split accounting and payout. Request log, route snapshot, settlement record, provider receipt, and audit log MUST carry mutually reconcilable immutable values for at least `pool_id`, manifest version, manifest core digest, route snapshot id, provider identity fingerprint, buyer credential fingerprint, token counts, settlement timestamp, settlement mode, rate-card identity, and `split_execution_status` for the creator dispute window defined by the Creator Agreement. MVP settlement MUST preserve already-issued provider receipts, reject duplicate settlement for the same route snapshot id, and expose an audit query proving that the payout-ready queue contains zero records attributable to `revenue_split_bps` declared in the pool manifest.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:163:- `phase4-coordinator/internal/trustpool/status.go` builds closed-schema `macprovider.trustpool-status.v1` documents for authorized buyer accounts and for public readers only when a matching public-announcement approval exists for a non-candidate launch environment; it reports pool/creator/policy/control-plane membership counts/settlement/confidentiality fields, resolved retention-policy registry status/version/categories, omits member provider identities, redacts internal creator approval, Agreement, root-key, lifecycle-reason, and route-gate fields on the public surface, uses a 300-second freshness window, derives live route-time readiness and eligible member count from the routeable registry snapshot plus live provider-serving and binary-floor state on the served buyer/public endpoints, exposes `publicly_announced` only on the digest-approved public surface, and explicitly discloses that readiness is not a free-capacity promise and this is a Trusted Pool, not a Privacy Pool, anonymous-routing, zero-knowledge, or regulated-compliance claim.
specs/SPEC-043-trusted-pool-creator-onboarding.md:229:- 0.1.0 evidence update - Adds durable `root_compromise_frozen` events plus creator/admin emergency intake that still works while the creator is suspended. Generic `/events` append rejects this event type so freeze receipts stay server-stamped. Frozen root fingerprints and delegated manifest-authority key ids reject later nonce issuance and mutations with `root_compromise_freeze`. Isolated candidate observations for freeze and descendant-signer rejection may now be true; SPEC-043 stays pending. Normative version unchanged.
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:12:- Operator SCOPE reopen of D1 **only** as D1a: public buyers stay donation-only (no Stripe, no checkout, no cards). A named wholesale partner class MAY be billed by an operator-issued monthly postpaid USD statement from metered settled usage on paid SKUs. Free SKUs are $0 to the partner. Provider `ComputeCredits` 90% `provider_share` still accrues for free and paid SKU work.
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:17:**Change log v0.6.5 (SPEC-041 composition):** Relay-blind work uses the existing quota, journal, request-log, refund, finality, delivered-output, ordinary provider-earnings, payment, and payout-readiness formulas. Billable input is the lesser of reported input and its clear cap; unknown input is zero, never a ciphertext estimate. Output remains bounded by clear output cap and delivered-output rules. Durable relay context must recover to at most one settlement. The draft pilot is excluded only from positive SPEC-022 receipt/verified-work reward claims and may run only under SPEC-022 off/observe; enforce rejects before quota. No arithmetic or ledger owner changes.

specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:653:**Operator decision:** Public D1 remains **D**. A named wholesale partner class (OpenRouter join on the live pool) MAY be billed by an operator-issued monthly postpaid USD statement derived from metered settled usage on **paid** SKUs. Free SKUs are $0 to the partner. Provider credits still follow D3/D5 `ComputeCredits` at 90% `provider_share` for both free and paid SKU work; Malibu absorbs free-SKU partner cost the same way it absorbs donation-tier public usage. Still no Stripe, no checkout, no card collection, no auto top-up.
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:656:- Wholesale statements MUST be generated from coordinator `request_log` settled usage keyed by partner `account_id` + UTC calendar month. Identifiers MUST be `wholesale_statement_id` / `wholesale_period_statements` (not `invoice_id`, not `buyer_invoice`).
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:664:**Operator decision:** **A** - real-time accrue + weekly settlement-ready batch UTC Monday 00:00; `settlement.cadence_days: 7` in coordinator.yaml; in-process goroutine (no new ops surface).
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:677:**Operator decision:** **B** - $0.50 nominal = 500,000 credits (using 1 credit = $0.000001); `settlement.min_payout_credits: 500000` in coordinator.yaml; sub-threshold credits roll forward to next weekly cycle (`settled=0`); configurable for SPEC-007 gas calibration.
specs/SPEC-005-billing.md:695:**Operator decision:** **A** - hard limit at account-day boundary per SPEC-006 section 17.7 (not re-implemented in SPEC-005); provider is credited for actual reported usage regardless of buyer quota state; provider is never zero-credited for legitimate completed work.
